abstract: We review the main ROADM subsystem technologies, and propose a 40-channel PLC-based ROADM subsystem that exhibits ultra-low power consumption and compact size, while meeting the requirements for high optical performance, high reliability, and low cost.

articleTitle: Fair routing and wavelength assignment in all-optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We introduce new routing and wavelength assignment algorithms for all-optical networks without wavelength conversion which accommodate calls with higher quality of service and more fairly than traditional algorithms without sacrificing low blocking probabilities.

articleTitle: A comparison between multi-level modulation formats: 21.4-Gbit/s RZ-DQPSK and POLMUX-RZ-DPSK
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally compare the nonlinear tolerance of DWDM 21.4-Gbit/s RZ-DQPSK and 21.4-Gbit/s POLMUX-RZ-DPSK modulation over an 800-km SSMF straight-line. We show that the small depolarization penalty of POLMUX-RZ-DPSK makes it a possible alternative to RZ-DQPSK modulation for next-generation transmission.

articleTitle: Directly-modulated DS-DBR tunable laser for uncooled C-band WDM system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A tunable DS-DBR laser is demonstrated for uncooled WDM C-band channel generation with tight spacing (50 GHz) and low thermal drift (plusmn 2.5 GHz) up to 70degC. 2.5 Gb/s direct modulation with transmission over a 75 km link is achieved

articleTitle: Synchronizing optical data and electrical control planes in asynchronous optical packet switches
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the use of optical payload envelope detection in a 40 Gbit/s asynchronous optical packet switch to synchronize the optical data and electrical control planes. Measurements show 100% envelope recovery over an 8.5 dB packet power dynamic range.

articleTitle: The value of multiple degree ROADMs on metropolitan network economics
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare alternative ROADM network architectures through a study based on real LEC data. We show that optimally deployed higher-degree ROADMs with optical bypass and grooming can simultaneously reduce the cost of both the optical and SONET layers.

articleTitle: All-optical packet switching by MMI-BLD optical flip-flop
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated novel all-optical packet switching using all-optical flip-flop multimode interference bistable laser diodes and all-optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer switches. Error-free operation for output 10-Gb/s optical packets from the switch was obtained with no power penalty.

articleTitle: Managing and controlling GMPLS network resources for grid applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Inter-working between GMPLS network and grid computing application through Web-services interface is demonstrated for the first time. Lambda LSP-based network resource virtualization and scheduling techniques successfully achieves nation-wide grid computing environment with advance reservation operation.

articleTitle: High-rate photon-efficient laser communications with near single photon/bit receiver sensitivities
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical communication systems with sensitivities approaching a single photon/bit can be realized by combining near-quantum-limited optically-preamplified receiver performance with energy-efficient modulation and coding. Potential applications include average-power-limited photon-starved links where channel bandwidth is readily available.

articleTitle: Performance characterization of components with phase ripple for different 40 Gb/s formats
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the relation between component phase ripple and system penalty by measuring the OSNR penalties with 40 Gb/s NRZ, RZ and CSRZ formats, and discuss the best estimator for the penalty.

articleTitle: Petabit-per-second routers: optical vs. electronic implementations
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare optical and electronic buffers and switches for use in future 1-Pb/s routers. Based on the scaling properties of optical and electronic devices, we conclude that electronics will be the technology of choice for future Pb/s routers

articleTitle: Optical add/drop multiplexer with asymmetric bandwidth allocation and dispersion compensation hybrid 10-Gb/s and 40-Gb/s DWDM transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a novel OADM having asymmetric bandwidth to optimally support hybrid 10-Gb/s and 40-Gb/s DWDM transmission with 50-GHz spacing. 10-Gb/s RZ-OOK and 40-Gb/s DPSK signals are passed through multiple OADMs with moderate penalty.

articleTitle: Fiber designs for reducing stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper discusses stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) in optical fibers. Theoretical approach for analyzing the SBS in fiber is described. Different fiber design methods for reducing the SBS effect are presented.

articleTitle: Phase conjugation for increased system robustness
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The transmission performance of optical phase conjugation (OPC) is assessed with a special focus on the combination with the RZ-DQPSK modulation format. We show that when OPC is employed, significant performance improvement is obtained compared to conventional DCF based transmission.

articleTitle: Long-haul 40 Gb/s RZ-DPSK transmission with long repeater spacing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 40 Gb/s RZ-DPSK signals were successfully transmitted over 4,920 km with 110 km repeater spacing using only single stage C-band EDFAs. The performance of 40 Gb/s and 10 Gb/s RZ-DPSK was compared. Q-factor fluctuations are an issue for 40 Gb/s systems.

articleTitle: Improved polarization-nulling technique for monitoring OSNR in WDM network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a simple method to improve the polarization-nulling technique by using a tunable optical filter. The results show that the proposed technique can monitor OSNR accurately even when the signal is significantly depolarized due to the nonlinear birefringence.

articleTitle: Experimental results of EDC based receivers for 2400 ps/nm at 10.7 Gb/s for emerging telecom standards
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Extensive experimental work with electronic dispersion compensation, a critical new technology for Metro 10G networks, was carried out by multiple companies. The results supporting 2400 ps/nm link are presented and form the bases for emerging Telecom application codes.

articleTitle: All-optical format conversion from NRZ-OOK to RZ-BPSK using SOA-MZI wavelength converter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel all-optical NRZ-OOK/RZ-BPSK format conversion scheme, using cross-phase modulation effects in a MZI-SOA. We experimentally demonstrate error free conversion at 10.7 Gb/s with a negative power penalty of 2.9 dB

articleTitle: Opto-electrical filter for 40 Gb/s optical single sideband signal generation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An opto-electrical filter for 40 Gb/s optical single sideband (OSSB) signal generation is experimentally shown. The improved dispersion tolerance of the OSSB signal is experimentally assessed with and without a simple electrical dispersive line

articleTitle: Low phase-noise 40 GHz optical pulses from a self-starting electroabsorption-modulator-based optoelectronic oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an optoelectronic oscillator using an electroabsorption modulator to generate a low phase-noise 40 GHz optical pulse train. The oscillator has a measured phase noise of -100 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset from the carrier.

articleTitle: Polymer saturable absorber materials in 1.5 /spl mu/m band using PMMA and ps with single-wall carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report thick saturable absorber materials using PMMA and PS polymers with single-wall carbon nanotubes. These materials were easily optically polished on both surfaces and a 171 fs pulse was successfully generated in a passively mode-locked fiber laser.

articleTitle: Compact RZ-DPSK transmitter applying a phaseCOMB laser as carved source
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A RZ-DPSK transmitter is assembled applying a phaseCOMB laser as compact and spectrally efficient carved source. System performance is evaluated at 40 Gbit/s and error free transmission over 160 km standard single-mode fibre is demonstrated

articleTitle: Suppression of Raman-induced pilot tone crosstalk using optical allpass filters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new type of optical allpass filter useful for mitigation of Raman-induced crosstalk among pilot tones and similar low-frequency labels. Crosstalk rejection was characterized in a 40-wavelength lab test system, and shown to agree well with theory.

articleTitle: Efficient design and modeling of doped-fiber amplifiers and lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We showed that our specialist simulation platform allows for the efficient design and analysis of new high-power doped fiber applications. In particular, we discussed modeling and design issues of high-power CW and Q-switched Er, Yb and co-doped fiber lasers and amplifiers using core or cladding pumping. Simulation results have been compared with published experimental data.

articleTitle: Dynamic bandwidth allocation algorithm for next generation access network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we propose a simple dynamic bandwidth allocation (DBA) algorithm that improves EPON's performance and introduce the analytic model of our proposed algorithm and prove theoretically our algorithm to be asymptotically stable as well as through simulation results. Simulation results also show our proposed bandwidth allocation algorithm provides higher bandwidth efficiency and lower queuing delay of ONU than other conventional allocation algorithms in EPON.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of all-optical "missing chip detection" to alleviate near-far effect in O-CDMA systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel receiver design for O-CDMA systems based on all-optical missing-chip detection. Penalty due to near-far effect is reduced by >8 dB compared to the conventional receiver and the interference-tolerance is increased by >6 dB.

articleTitle: Spinning-induced stress distribution affecting beatlength in constantly spun fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The interplay of fiber drawing parameters and constant spinning process, affecting beatlength in spun fibers, is theoretically investigated. Experimental validation is provided by tomographic stress characterization on fibers spun at different rates and drawing speeds

articleTitle: High extinction ratio pulse generation from FM signal by using dispersion imbalanced fiber loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A dispersion imbalanced fiber loop mirror is used to compress the FM modulated optical signal to pulse and improve its extinction ratio simultaneously. The pulse-width is adjustable by controlling the driving RF power.

articleTitle: High-availability in multipoint to multipoint Ethernet for the delivery of triple play services
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Ethernet has become a key technology in the development of new end-user applications. One such application is triple play, which offers a service bundle including voice, data and video services. These are offered over the same infrastructure, which means that the service provider needs to take into consideration the combination of the QoS and availability requirements of all individual services combined. A way of offering these services is through the creation of a common broadcast domain through VPLS. This enables multipoint to multipoint connectivity, effectively emulating an extended LAN over the transport infrastructure. While RPR is capable of providing the levels of network availability required to offer triple play services, consistently with customer SLAs, it does not offer any way of protecting against unidirectional physical layer failures in the downstream direction (i.e. the interface between the video server and the local RPR node). VPLS RFI offers a method to propagate a fault indication to all remote nodes part of the VPLS infrastructure. It relies on the generation and propagation of RSVP-TE LOS signaling to all members of the VPLS, resulting in a switchover to an alternate VPLS protection domain. VPLS RFI in combination of RPR, offer high levels of availability in triple play networks, consistent with service level agreements.

articleTitle: Employing slow polarization scrambling to improve performances for ultra-long haul DWDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using slow polarization scrambling to improve transmission performance simultaneously for multichannel of deployment ready DWDM system with reconfigurable OADM nodes is presented. It showed that the power fluctuation and maximum PreFEC BER can be reduced by using slow polarization scrambling.

articleTitle: Photonic signal processing of high-speed signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photonic signal processing offers the prospect of high sampling frequencies, overcoming inherent electronic limitations. Recent new methods in wideband signal processing using optical delay lines are described, including novel interference mitigation filters without phase noise

articleTitle: Negative feedback optical amplifier based on cross-gain modulation in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A negative feedback optical amplifier was demonstrated using negative feedback based on cross-gain modulation in an erbium-doped fiber amplifier. The optical amplifier is capable of providing an output signal whose gain is stabilized and controlled automatically

articleTitle: Stable multiwavelength actively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber ring laser based on distributed dispersion cavity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel stable multiwavelength actively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber ring laser was demonstrated using distributed dispersion cavity. Simultaneous generation of wavelength tunable 10 GHz pulses up to four different wavelengths was achieved

articleTitle: Analysis of high-performance near-ballistic uni-traveling-carrier photodiode at a 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: State-of-the-art performance: high responsivity (1.04 A/W), wide bandwidth (~50 GHz), and high saturation current-bandwidth product (over 1280 mA-GHz/40 GHz), of near-ballistic uni-traveling-carrier photodiode can be attributed to near-ballistic transport and ac capacitance reduction, which has been verified by our measurement and device-modeling

articleTitle: 10G-enabled optical network architecture directions for video, voice and data: an MSO perspective
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We discuss the characteristics of a converged, 10G-enabled, DWDM optical network architecture used to provide carrier-grade service availability, resilience, and protection for a variety of multimedia commercial and entertainment services. By exploiting advances in 10G technology and overlaying OSI layer 2/3 with layer-1 photonics, the network can scale efficiently and provide the most flexibility for current and future service delivery.

articleTitle: Data transmission through a 1014-channel two-dimensional array wavelength demultiplexer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 1/spl times/1014 channel wavelength demultiplexer with 50 GHz pitch and a 594 nm total bandwidth. The hybrid AWG/grating produced a 26/spl times/39 array of wavelength-demultiplexed spots measured by an InGaAs camera and by a scanned output fiber used to sample the output. Insertion loss was <10 dB for all channels measured within the 1270 nm to 1700 nm operating range (700 total channels). BER measurements show a 0.1 dB power penalty at 10 GB/s.

articleTitle: Performance characteristics for delivering Ethernet private line service in a multi-vendor SONET environment
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Ethernet-based services continue to grow in popularity as customers use the technology for wide area network connectivity. To meet customer demand for Ethernet private line (EPL) services, Verizon has developed a comprehensive approach that uses existing legacy SONET and NG-SONET equipment to deliver a less expensive and more efficient alternative to DS3 for WAN connections to customer sites. Verizon's customers expect its EPL service to perform similar to existing TDM-based private line services, with all the transmission characteristics of a SONET network. However, Verizon's NG-SONET vendors have different Ethernet over SONET (EoS) implementations, and these differences have made it difficult for Verizon to establish performance benchmarks and guarantee service levels. To address this challenge, Verizon is defining a set of standard EPL service attributes that will be used to benchmark Ethernet and NG-SONET performance in a multi-vendor EoS environment.

articleTitle: Replicated polymer waveguides for access applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A replication technology for fabricating polymer optical waveguides has been developed. With this technology, coupler modules are successfully demonstrated with practical characteristics for low cost access applications. And V-groove integration onto those devices is introduced.

articleTitle: Progress in DWDM deployment in MCI's North American network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: MCI owns network facilities in more than 140 countries and over 2,800 cities. MCI is in the midst of an ultra-long haul build of the North American network. This paper outlines MCI's plan and progress on this front.

articleTitle: Design of multi-tier networks to support data-intensive applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: There is an increasing interest in transferring large terabyte and petabyte sized files to support scientific and government applications. Such applications require dynamic acquisition of dedicated and deterministic data services. GMPLS networks under development can address this demand.

articleTitle: 10 GHz dark-optical-comb injection-mode-locked semiconductor optical amplifier fiber laser with 400 fs and 30 nm tunable pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 30 nm wavelength-tunable backward dark-optical-comb injection-mode-locked semiconductor optical amplifier fiber laser with pedestal-free and transform-limited pulsewidth of 180 fs and 400 fs at 1 GHz and 10 GHz, respectively, is reported after high-order soliton compression with maximum pulse compression ratio of up to 80.

articleTitle: Local structure analysis of Er in Er-doped fiber with Al co-doping
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Local structure of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> in the Er-doped optical fiber (EDF) was explored by the X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) measurement. We have successfully observed variations of Er-O coordination number and Er-O distance by changing the Al concentration

articleTitle: Challenges in testing resilient packet ring
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Resilient packet ring (RPR) is a metropolitan area network technology for data transfer based on ring configuration and is standardized as IEEE 802.17. RPR testing is challenging as it combines best of SONET networks and data networks. The paper provides guidelines for generation of standard compliant test suite, recommends simulated environments for RPR testing and puts forward a strategy for automation of RPR testing. The paper describes various stages of RPR testing and the challenges considering entire project cycle.

articleTitle: Multi-hop optical label swapping using synchronous phase modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate cascaded optical label swapping using synchronous phase modulation without wavelength conversion via a re-circulating loop to emulate multi-hop networks. We find the power penalties for both label and payload are below 1 dB after 5 hops.

articleTitle: Tunable gain tilt compensator using adiabatic mode multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We built gain tilt compensator in silica on silicon using adiabatic mode multiplexer and y-branch based Mach-Zehnder interferometer. Process and design tolerant building blocks allow flexibility in achieving required response, either normally bright or tilted, and excellent optical performance.

articleTitle: High-resolution control of optical phase for code-empowered networking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The ability to modify the individual optical phases of close-spaced, phase-locked laser lines underlies spectrally phase encoded optical-CDMA networks offering signal obscurity and scrambling, passive code-exchange and routing, and spectral efficiency comparable to DWDM

articleTitle: Simple improvement of error correction capability of standard FEC using repeated trial-and-error method
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Error correction capability of standard RS(255,239)-code is optimized within the limits of hard-decision decoding. An improvement of about 0.2 dB is achieved without noticeable increase in decoding complexity

articleTitle: Optical networking in non-telecommunications applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This presentation provides an overview of various analog and digital applications, network architectures, and technology trends in various ongoing industrial, scientific, and government-related application environments.

articleTitle: Stabilization of an actively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber ring laser by multi-harmonic phase modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate actively mode-locked operation of a fiber laser using a novel multi-harmonic phase modulation technique. By mixing two harmonics of the fundamental cavity frequency to drive a phase modulator, improved stability performance is observed.

articleTitle: Novel tone-like polarization modulation-based encoding method experimental demonstrated on a 10 G data channel over 130 Km
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a novel encoding method and feasibility demonstration using tone-like polarization modulation onto an independently modulated OC-192 optical signal for supervisory signaling within optical networks. We demonstrate experimentally error free performance for 10 Gbps NRZ and 155 Mbs polarization modulated signal

articleTitle: Polarization and bit-length independent all-optical logic gate based active correlator for bit serial label processing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate correlation of bit-serial labels in optical label switching networks using an all-optical semiconductor optical amplifier based XOR gate. The proposed scheme does not require precise phase maintenance, is scalable, and is polarization independent.

articleTitle: Impact of multi-port card diversity constraints in mesh optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We model and measure the impact of multi-port cards and circuit-pack diversity constraints on the routing of protected lightpaths in optical networks and the resulting network capacity. We describe an offline routing and channel assignment algorithm combined with a multi-port card configuration algorithm, and experiments with these algorithms on various network designs. We show in particular that the impact is negligible, even in the case of shared-mesh protection architectures protecting against single multi-port card failures.

articleTitle: Time-spreading/wavelength-hopping OCDMA using PLC encoder/decoder with large spread factor
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We fabricated an integrated-optic encoder/decoder with a spread factor of 48 for time-spreading/wavelength-hopping optical CDMA (the largest number reported for this CDMA). We successfully carried out a 2.5 Gbit/s transmission with plural users using the devices

articleTitle: An optically pumped silicon evanescent laser operating continuous wave at 60/spl deg/C
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a silicon evanescent laser operating CW up to 60/spl deg/C. The laser operates at 1568 nm with a maximum fiber-coupled output power of 4.5 mW. Devices are fabricated with silicon waveguides bonded to AlGaInAs quantum wells.

articleTitle: Spin profiles reconstruction in low-PMD fibers by long range polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Polarization-sensitive optical coherence tomography is proved an efficient nondestructive technique for spin profile reconstruction along spun fiber coils, allowing birefringence parameter spatial evolution to be recovered from Stokes analysis of backscattered light, with sub-centimetric resolution.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of the continuous tuning of microwave photonic filters by sinusoidal modulation of the filter coefficients
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show the results of a technique to tune continuously the resonances of the microwave photonic filters are shifted by changing the weight of the optical taps. It improves the performance of the cited filters.

articleTitle: Optical demultiplexing of up to 200 Gb/s data employing asymmetric switching pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A detailed study on all-optical switching based on one switching pulse edge through cross-phase modulation was carried out. Optical demultiplexing of up to 200 Gb/s data has been demonstrated by merely using 11.7 ps asymmetric switching pulses.

articleTitle: Bend-induced distortion in microstructure and solid fibers with very large mode area
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Simulations show that bend-induced mode distortion should have a major impact on nonlinearities for fibers with very large cores, relevant to high-power amplifiers and lasers. Designs resistant to bend-induced distortion are proposed

articleTitle: High-speed broadband polarization-independent optical clock recovery in a silicon detector
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have recently successfully used a silicon detector for optical clock recovery at 1.55 /spl mu/m and speeds up to 80 Gb/s. We report here a novel optical dithering scheme that eliminates polarization dependence in the system and improves the dynamic range without introducing additional jitter in the recovered clock.

articleTitle: Frequency stability in high speed frequency switching of digitally tunable laser using ladder filter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A monolithically integrated digitally tunable ring laser has been developed that employs a ladder filter and a ring resonator. The ladder filter selects one channel from the periodic channels of the ring resonator and the stable device performance is achieved by adopting a chirped ladder filter with one dominant passband. The device is capable of 34-channel (100-GHz spacing) digitally tunable laser operation and the sidemode suppression ratio is more than 40 dB. The switching time for any wavelength is less than 10 nsec and the frequency drift caused by the thermal transient is less than 500 MHz

articleTitle: High power fiber oscillators and amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Self-similar propagation of similariton and cubicon pulses in optical fibers is reviewed. Asymptotic pulse solutions are obtained in the presence of self-phase modulation, gain and gain narrowing, allowing for the generation of high energy pulses in fiber oscillators and amplifiers

articleTitle: Dilute nitride lasers and photodetectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Dilute nitride alloys are attractive candidates for lasers and detectors between 1.25 and 1.6 /spl mu/m. We have demonstrated the first low-threshold continuous-wave 1.55 /spl mu/ GaAs-based lasers and the first > 1.5 /spl mu/m monolithic VCSELs using GaInNAsSb quantum wells as the active region and photodetectors based upon similar alloys.

articleTitle: Silicon impact-ionization multiplier for optical detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a current multiplier which can be operated with either silicon or indium-gallium-arsenide photodiodes for optical detection. Current gains above 100 along with pre-amplified leakage currents of less than 2 nA were measured.

articleTitle: Fibre core shape transitions for optical interfacing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Transitions in core shape are formed in photonic crystal fibres by differential pressurisation of the holes and localised heating. Low-loss anamorphic transitions to rectangular and annular cores are formed, and improved coupling from diode lasers to fibres thereby demonstrated.

articleTitle: The role of MPLS in delivering triple-play services
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Providing triple play services (voice, video and data) for residential consumers is the key ingredient of many carriers' strategies for increased revenue and competitiveness. To fend off the attacks of cable operators and competitive carriers on their core business (telephony), carriers are striking back on the MSOs' traditional turf - video with enhanced service offerings. At the same time, the war goes on in Internet access services, with increased bandwidth and declining prices. Wireline carriers have begun to offer triple-play services while leveraging new digital subscribe line (DSL) technologies such as ADSL2+ and VDSL2 on their exiting copper infrastructure. Other operators have started to deploy fiber to the home in order to boost the capacity of the services per residence. This paper describes the different methods of delivering an aggregation solution for these access technologies. It describes routing-based aggregation solutions were first used by operators to deliver triple play services and explores their limitations, that. Later, this paper describes the migration of the networks to an MPLS-based aggregation solution, the problems it solves and the benefits it delivers.

articleTitle: 160 GHz reciprocating optical modulator using uniform fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated stable 160 GHz clock signal generation, by using a reciprocating optical modulator with uniform fiber Bragg gratings having narrow passbands adjacent to reflection bands, which enables effective generation of high-order sideband components.

articleTitle: Room-temperature tunable multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber laser based on degenerate four-wave mixing effect in dispersion-shifted fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a stably tunable multiwavelength erbium-doped fiber laser based on degenerate four-wave mixing in dispersion-shifted fibers at room temperature. The lasing wavelength can be continuously controlled by the polarization controller.

articleTitle: Frequency-shifted interferometer and its applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a frequency-shifted interferometer and demonstrate its various applications, including fiber length and dispersion measurement, multiple weak reflection sites locating along a fiber link. This could be a useful interrogation technique for sensor multiplexing

articleTitle: Multiple phase-shift all-fibre DFB lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A double (2 times pi/2) phase-shifted Er/Yb fibre DFB laser shows a 50% reduction of the shift in lasing wavelength and a 10% reduction of the linewidth, compared to standard single phase-shifted fibre DFB designs

articleTitle: Coaxial laser diode module with a front facet power monitor photodiode
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel structure of coaxial LD module with a high-speed front facet power monitor PD was successfully developed. The PD current variation was ten times smaller than a conventional LD module. This module is suitable for automatic extinction ratio control.

articleTitle: Characterizing fiber patchcord bending effects
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The bend-loss performance of singlemode patchcords is critical to data integrity in high-speed (10 Gigabits/second) systems. Patchcords used in high power networks must operate without sustaining damage or creating hazardous conditions.

articleTitle: Effect of air hole size on transmission characteristics of fiber Bragg gratings written in holey fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We discuss effect of air hole size on transmission characteristics of fiber Bragg gratings written in holey fiber. The strain and temperature sensitivities of grating strongly depend on the air hole size of holey fibers

articleTitle: Baseband optical down-sampling for high-performance analog links
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A baseband optical down-sampling architecture is experimentally demonstrated where both inphase and quadrature channel are directly accessed using two integrated dual mode-locked lasers. A 2-dB conversion penalty is obtained for a 50 Mbaud QPSK-modulated 2.5 GHz RF signal.

articleTitle: The use of multi-fiber ferrules in FTTP applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: With the long-awaited arrival of the fiber-to-the-premises initiative (FTTP), there has been a focused effort to devise the most effective solutions for construction of the needed outside plant infrastructure. The outcome of this activity is a preconnectorized solution for the distribution network based on the MT ferrule. The main advantages of the MT-based solution include lower initial capital investment per home passed, speed of deployment, and a reduced need for precise field measurements of the cable plant. The lower capital requirement for service providers results from the ability to delay in time the placement of the network access point terminal with its associated adapters and pigtails. The speed of deployment advantage comes from the compact nature of the resulting tap point. An overmold process is used to provide a small, flexible solution that works well with outside plant installation practices. Due to its flexibility, it can be routed easily. The reduced need for field tap location measurement accuracy stems from the fact that one can now install the cable and measure exactly where the final terminal needs to be because of a flexible tether length that is part of the design. An additional advantage attributable to the use of the tether is the ability to use whatever enclosure solution makes sense in a given application without regard for whether or not it passes through a sheave wheel. The proposed paper will cover the evolution of the terminal distribution system for FTTP networks and discuss the capability and performance of the new MT-based system. Test data on a new multifiber ferrule based connector to Telcordia GR-3120 will be presented. Additional testing of the completed assembly to Telcordia GR-3122 will be presented.

articleTitle: High index contrast photonics components for data communication
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Microresonator-based high index contrast integrated optical components show promising performance for the demands of near-future optical networks. Experimental results of an ultra-compact reconfigurable OADM at 40 Gbit/s are presented in detail

articleTitle: Digital work design tools for FTTP
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Digital work design (DWD) tools have been applied to FTTP. An extensive ergonomic analysis of a new local convergence point (LCP) product, conducted in a 3D virtual world, has resulted in an improved product with reduced number of product design iterations. Application of these tools can reduce both labor costs and time-to-market and help ensure that network elements are "user friendly" and safe.

articleTitle: Enhancing link bundling performance in GMPLS transparent networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In transparent networks, link bundling (LB) trades off high resource utilization efficiency provided by detailed routing information advertisement for routing protocol scalability. The proposed GMPLS extension enhances LB resource utilization while preserving LB scalability.

articleTitle: Optical beat interference suppression using semiconductor optical amplifier in reflective semiconductor optical amplifier based WDM/SCM-passive optical network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We proposed a novel method suppressing the OBI noise in RSOA based WDM/SCM-PON. This is to use the SOA operated in gain saturation range, which acts as high pass filter. CNR increased up to 15 dB compared with that without using a SOA.

articleTitle: ASE-to-signal coupling limitations to generate hundreds to thousands of optical replica from a unique pulse
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An efficient design using a re-circulation fibre loop is proposed to generate huge amounts of pulse-shape replica, from one single pulse at 1053 nm. We analyze the limitations due to the ASE noise-to-signal sequential transfer.

articleTitle: All fiber dynamic gain equalizer based on a twisted long period grating written by high frequency CO/sub 2/ laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel dynamic gain equalizer for flattening Er-doped fiber amplifiers based on a twisted long period fiber grating (LPFG) induced by high-frequency CO/sub 2/ laser pulses is reported, for the first time to our knowledge. Experimental results show that its transverse load sensitivity is up to 0.34 dB/(g.mm--1) when a 100 mm long fiber with a LPFG in the middle of it is twisted about 20 rad/m, which is 7 times higher than that of a torsion-free LPFG. In addition, it is found that the strong orientation-dependence of the transverse load sensitivity of the torsion-free LPFG reported previously has been weakened considerably. Therefore, such a dynamic gain equalizer based on the unique transverse load characteristics of the twisted LPFG provides a much larger adjustable range and makes packaging of the gain equalizer much easier. A demonstration has been carried out to flatten an Er-doped fibre amplifier to /spl plusmn/0.5 dB over a 32 nm bandwidth.

articleTitle: Low crosstalk demodulators for 42.8 Gb/s WDM DPSK
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new type of optical demodulator is proposed to reduce the channel crosstalk in dense WDM DPSK systems. It can relieve the strong filtering condition required by transmitting 42.8 Gb/s signals over 50 GHz ITU grids.

articleTitle: Hollow-core radially-chirped Bragg fiber for quasi-metallic photonic bandgap light confinement
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze hollow-core radially-chirped Bragg fiber which propagates light via oscillatory modal evolution and lens relay refocusing with 55 mum full-period. Our design shows both photonic bandgap light confinement in an aperiodic geometry, and quasi-metallic waveguide properties

articleTitle: A simple tapered bismuth-based nonlinear optical fiber for low-loss coupling to single-mode silica fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Spot-size-converter for low loss coupling of Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-based nonlinear optical fiber is proposed. The tapered structure for mode-field expansion is constructed by a simple fabrication procedure. The experimental results show the improvement of the coupling efficiency.

articleTitle: CO/sub 2/-laser fabricated long-period grating sensors in graded-index multimode fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report long-period grating fabricated in a graded-index multimode fiber by deforming the geometry of the fiber periodically with a focused CO/sub 2/-laser beam. The sensing applications of such multimode fiber long-period gratings are proposed.

articleTitle: Nanotechnology for Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The paper reviews the application of nanotechnology in optical fiber communications, infrared detectors and photovoltaics. The use of PbS quantum dot and silicon nanocrystals are possible materials that can be used in these fields

articleTitle: BER performance on access network using centralized light sources and single mode + multi mode fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An access network using a centralized light sources (CLS) and multi mode fiber (MMF) is proposed and verified using BER measurements. Results show that we can implement CLS based PON using currently existing MMF infrastructure.

articleTitle: Systems integration & testing challenges for generation optical transport networks (NGOTNs)
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we discuss systems integration & testing challenges for NGOTNs. After an overview of the architecture, we discuss the issues we have experienced in the course of our evaluations. We end with recommendations to the vendor community.

articleTitle: Optical modulator bias monitoring with two-photon-absorption in Si-APD in advanced modulation formats optical transmitters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated more sensitive monitoring of modulator bias point with two-photon-absorption in Si-APD. For NRZ, RZ and CS-RZ signals, the sensitivity with TPA monitoring is at least double of that with power monitoring.

articleTitle: High power cladding-pumped Raman fiber laser with true single-mode output at 1660 nm
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a 10 W continuous-wave cladding-pump Raman fiber laser with single-mode output at 1660 nm pumped by a high-power Er:Yb fiber amplifier. The laser threshold was 6.5 W and its slope efficiency was 67%.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of postnonlinearity compensation in a multi-span DPSK transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate performance improvement in a multi-span 10 Gb/s DPSK transmission by employing postnonlinearity compensation. Significant improvements in BER were obtained for both dispersion managed soliton and quasi-linear transmission.

articleTitle: Optical processing based on spectral line-by-line shaping on a phase modulated CW laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate optical processing based on spectral line-by-line pulse shaping on a phase modulated CW laser and show various applications including CW-to-pulse conversion, width/wavelength tunable return-to-zero pulse generation, pulse-to-CW conversion, wavelength conversion and microwave photonics

articleTitle: OSNR enhancement using a novel pump-wavelength detuning scheme for forward-pumped distributed Raman amplification in a 40 Gb/s-based WDM in-line amplifier transmission system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: OSNR enhancement by using a novel pump-wave length detuning scheme for forward-pumped distributed Raman amplification in a 40 Gb/s-based L-band WDM in-line amplifier transmission system is experimentally verified for the first time.

articleTitle: FSK-WDM to IM-OTDM conversion for fiber-to-the-premises access networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a FSK-WDM to IM-OTDM conversion system, based on a MZI wavelength converter. The FSK channels data rate is 500 Mbps, while error and power penalty free conversion to 5 Gbps IM-OTDM is reported. Operation at 10 Gbps is also shown.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity-tolerant in-band OSNR monitoring for synchronous traffic using gated-signal RF spectral analysis
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a new in-band OSNR monitoring scheme using RF spectral analysis of gated framing-signal of synchronous traffic. The proposed technique is simple and robust to fiber-nonlinearity induced polarization rotation in WDM systems.

articleTitle: Waveguide amplifier for all-optical WDM network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a gain clamped waveguide amplifier design suitable for all-optical WDM networks. We show negligible extra noise figure penalty and strong immunity from channel reconfiguration or network failure. This configuration can be fully integrated yielding compact low-cost mass production

articleTitle: Multi-channel dispersion compensator based on a flexible structure
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Multi-channel dispersion compensator is demonstrated based on the strongly-chirped, phase-shifted sampled Bragg gratings. Wideband dispersion compensators with different channel spacing, dispersion, and dispersion slope can be obtained with a single conventional phase mask

articleTitle: Comparison of two optical switching architectures to provide a broadband connection to train passengers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: To provide high bandwidth services to train passengers, a dedicated broadband network along the railways is proposed. By means of optical switching, we want to limit the handover times and so increase the available bandwidth.

articleTitle: All-optical ASK header and DPSK payload separator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an all-optical scheme to separate ASK header and DPSK payload based on cross-gain-modulation and nonlinear polarization rotation in semiconductor optical amplifiers. The scheme is automatic and does not require any external header detector.

articleTitle: Solving wireless backhaul issues with optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The increasing demand for wireless services is calling attention to perceived weaknesses in the tower backhaul. Wireless service providers place the blame for 60% - 80% of service outages on problems with the backhaul. Optical fiber offers an immediate solution to performance and operational issues. Advances in optical fiber cable and equipment have reduced the cost of deploying optical fiber links while still providing backwards compatibility with existing fiber infrastructure and forward compatibility with 3G wireless systems.

articleTitle: Model-based optimal optical network planning and operations
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: LDI Oasys for optimal optical network planning and traffic engineering handles uncertain traffic forecasts, dynamic complex constraints, and customizable business objectives. In pilot applications, Oasys reduced equipment cost by 35% and increased revenue by 26%.

articleTitle: New operation scheme of SOA-MZI all-optical wavelength converter cancelling cross gain modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: New operation scheme of SOA-MZI all-optical wavelength converter by which effect of cross gain modulation is cancelled out utilizing bidirectional data signal input is proposed and experimentally verified for the first time.

articleTitle: Linear and nonlinear optical properties of single-mode As/sub 2/Se/sub 3/ chalcogenide fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical properties of single-mode As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Se<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> chalcogenide fibers are investigated for applications in the 1.55 mum wavelength range. The fiber exhibits large Kerr nonlinearity (gamma=954 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) and a large Brillouin gain coefficient of 6.2 times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> m/W, about 134 times larger than fused silica fiber

articleTitle: Waveguide amplifiers in sputtered films of Er/sup 3+/-doped chalcogenide glass
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the first chalcogenide glass waveguide amplifiers operating at a wavelength of 1.5 mum. The amplifiers, patterned in films of Er<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>-doped gallium lanthanum sulfide glass, exhibit a total internal gain of 6.7 dB (2.8 dB/cm)

articleTitle: Maximum survivability under multiple failures
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper investigates the maximum survivability problem in mesh networks with multiple failures. A heuristic algorithm is proposed to maximize the end-to-end survivability. Simulation results show that the algorithm proposed in this paper is always better than the bounds of two link-disjoint paths protection scheme.

articleTitle: High average power harmonically mode locked ring laser based on phosphate glass fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report passive harmonic mode locking of Er/Yr doped phosphate fiber ring laser. The laser can be mode-locked at repetition rates from 1.7 to 7.2 GHz producing pulses with durations from 300 fs to 570 fs and 1.1 W of average power.

articleTitle: Optical frequency-domain modal dispersion measurement in multimode fibers using intermodal interferometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A modal dispersion measurement technique for a multimode optical fiber using an intermodal interferometer and optical frequency-domain reflectometry (OFDR) technique is demonstrated. A few-mode PCF and a commercial MMF are prepared to measure modal dispersions using our measurement technique.

articleTitle: Efficient supercontinuum generation in a ultra compact silica highly nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: HNLF with 50 mum cladding and optimized dispersion for efficient supercontinuum generation is designed and fabricated. High quality SC light was generated by 1 km HNLF wound on outer diameter of phi50 mm with 100 mW input power

articleTitle: 2.5 dB sensitivity improvement by optimizing the driving voltage of an MZM and electrical filter bandwidth of optical duobinary transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We numerically and experimentally demonstrated that 100% driving voltage doesn't necessarily yield optimal results in duobinary systems. Compared with conventional condition, a 2.5 dB sensitivity improvement is obtained using 3 GHz LPFs with optimum voltage.

articleTitle: Link performance of SOA-based slow and fast light
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We perform simple link analysis simulations to assess the performance of an SOA generating slow and fast light via four wave mixing. Power penalty is calculated for various alpha parameter values and bit rates.

articleTitle: Sub-picosecond pulse generation at 134 GHz using a quantum dash-based Fabry-Perot laser emitting at 1.56 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on 800 fs pulse generation, at 134 GHz, using a Fabry-Perot quantum dash laser at 1.56 mum. A 50 kHz RF spectral linewidth at 42 GHz is also demonstrated

articleTitle: A polarization controller air-core photonic-bandgap fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the effects of twisting on the birefringence of an air-core fiber and demonstrate the first air-core fiber polarization controller, a simple device consisting of three short twisted fiber sections, with a 20-dB extinction ratio.

articleTitle: Accurate time transfer utilizing the synchronization in an SDH-network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A nationwide system for accurate time distribution is being developed, utilizing synchronization in an SDH-network. The first experimental results based on this technique are presented, performed on, but not limited to, STM-64.

articleTitle: Optical waveguide filters using nanophotonics
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Improvements in fabrication tools open new frontiers in photonic design. We describe a new generation of lithographically rendered, nano-structured, building-block, integrated diffractive devices providing advanced spectral filtering, multiplexing, and interconnection in various material formats

articleTitle: Scalable all-optical compression/decompression of variable length (40 to 1500 byte) packets
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on the first experimental demonstration of all-optical compression and decompression of variable length packets (40-1500 bytes), into fixed temporal sized packets using variable compression ratios. End-to-end (compression and decompression) packet BER was measured with a penalty of /spl sim/1.65 dB.

articleTitle: Fiber strain due to spin during draw
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Thermophysical property measurements in optical fibers have revealed that stress applied to fiber during the drawing process is recorded in the structure of the drawn fiber and fiber twisting during draw can be detected in these measurements

articleTitle: Enlargement of measurement range in a Brillouin optical correlation domain analysis system using double lock-in amplifiers and a single-sideband modulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel technique to enlarge the measurement range of a correlation-based fiber Brillouin distributed sensing system using double lock-in amplifiers and a single-sideband (SSB) modulator. In our work, the lock-in detection is applied to both a probe and a pump waves at different frequencies to effectively remove the noise induced by the backward reflection of the pump waves, and the SSB modulator is used to purify the probe wave by suppressing the other first-order sideband component. A 300-m measurement range with a 20-cm spatial resolution is achieved successfully without any optical filter.

articleTitle: Fiber parametric amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This study presents the principles behind a fiber parametric amplifier (FPA) operation. This includes the discussion of parametric amplification, four-wave mixing, phase conjugation, wavelength conversion, and optical regeneration due to gain saturation. FPA applications for quantum-optical systems and optical processing are also discussed

articleTitle: ULH systems with strong filters acting as amplitude regenerators
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: It is shown that strong optical filters that are included in a ULH system can suppress, or enhance amplitude noise depending on their positioning. Our study explains the improvement measured in a 60-span system with 10 band-limited DGEs. Understanding of the physical mechanism allows the realization of same and better performance improvement as in the previous work (Wiesnfeld et. al., 2005) with only 2, optimally positioned filters

articleTitle: A systematic study of supercontinuum generation at 1.06 /spl mu/m in holey fibers with dispersion flattened profiles
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the results of a systematic experimental and theoretical study of 1.06 /spl mu/m pumped supercontinuum generation in holey fibers with different flattened dispersion characteristics. We identify several different operating regimes characterised by the relative positions of the zero dispersion wavelengths.

articleTitle: Impact of four-wave-mixing on microwave filters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Bandpass notch filters based on a dual-wavelength SOA and Raman fiber ring laser both with equalized peak power are proposed and demonstrated experimentally. Four wave mixing effect on the notch filters has been discussed.

articleTitle: Dual-depletion-region electro-absorption modulator at 1.55 /spl mu/m wavelength for high-speed and low-driving-voltage performance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel electro-absorption modulator, which can not only release the trade-off between driving-voltage and bandwidth but also the burden imposed on downscaling size of high-speed EAM. The electrical-to-optical measurement show very convincing results

articleTitle: A new technique for dynamic gain profile control in a multi-wavelength backward-pumped discrete Raman amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and experimentally verify a new dynamic gain profile control technique for a multi-wavelength backward-pumped discrete Raman amplifier without using a channel monitor. We demonstrate up to 9 dB static power correction and a dynamic implementation.

articleTitle: Fiber optic sensor for simultaneous leak detection of hydrazine and nitrogen dioxide gases
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Hydrazine and nitrogen dioxide hypergolic propellants are hazardous gases. This paper experimentally demonstrates, for the first time to our knowledge, the development of a fiber optic sensor for simultaneous leak monitoring of both gases at room temperature and pressure.

articleTitle: Polarization insensitive wideband tunable dispersion compensator with integrated PLC type polarization diversity circuit
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a novel polarization insensitive wideband tunable dispersion compensator with integrated PLC type polarization diversity circuit and obtained tunable dispersion range of +/-100 ps/nm and operating bandwidth of 0.6 nm.

articleTitle: A nanophotonic 4/spl times/4 wavelength router in silicon-on-insulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 400/spl times/150 /spl mu/m/sup 2/ silicon-on-insulator 4/spl times/4 arrayed waveguide grating with 3.5 dB insertion loss, fabricated with CMOS technology. The device was pigtailed and used as a wavelength router in a 10 Gb/s reconfigurable optical backplane interconnect.

articleTitle: Waveguide amplifier design and integration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new level of waveguide integration, capable of producing complex integrated optical circuits custom-designed to meet specific end-user requirements, is demonstrated. We discuss in details the performance and applications of a waveguide amplifier, a crucial building block in our library of optical elements. New circuits, such as an amplified reconfigurable add-drop module, are shown as examples of optical integration

articleTitle: Impulse response measurements using optical low coherence reflectometry with tunable source
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A recently proposed technique is used for the first time to measure the complex impulse response of fiber gratings (KL=0.5-3) and a DFB laser. Good agreement with independent spectral measurement and spatial resolution of ~30 mum are obtained

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s WDM-PON upstream transmission using injection-locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate, for the first time, a 10 Gb/s upstream transmission using Fabry-Perot laser diodes (FP-LD) remotely injection-locked by coherent feed light from the central office. Experimental results show that transmission over a 10-km single mode feeder fiber incurs power penalty of 1.1 dB and up to 16 cavity modes of the FP-LD can be injection-locked.

articleTitle: Tunable optical add-drop multiplexer based on silicon photonic wire waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A wavelength tunable optical add-drop multiplexer based on silicon photonic wire waveguides with Bragg-grating-reflectors was demonstrated by tuning the dropping wavelength through thermooptic effect. A 6.6-nm dropping wavelength shift was obtained at a 0.82-W heating power. For the device that is presently polarization-dependent, the 3-dB channel-dropping bandwidth was 0.4 nm and the extinction ratio at the dropping wavelength for port THROUGH was better than 17 dB for assuming 1.6-nm wavelength spacing dense wavelength-division multiplexing. The average tuning speed was about 200 /spl mu/s.

articleTitle: Bi-doped silica fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A new type of fiber laser - Bi-doped silica fiber laser has been proposed and realized for the first time. The laser generation was observed in the spectral region of 1150-1300 nm. The fibers were fabricated by MCVD technique.

articleTitle: High power single-frequency Yb doped fiber amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review the recent dramatic advances in high power single-frequency Yb doped fiber amplifiers and discuss fundamental aspects and future prospects. We present up-to-date experimental results with particular attention to cladding-pumped, refined power amplifier regimes.

articleTitle: A new high-power and low-RIN Raman pump laser for improved performance in long-span unrepeated WDM transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a high-power and low-noise laser for effective first- and higher-order co-pumping in distributed Raman amplifiers. Experiments at 10 Gb/s, also confirmed by simulations, point out RIN-penalty free transmission up to 25 dB of co-propagating on-off Raman gain.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity and dispersion control in small core lead silicate holey fibers by structured element stacking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a new fabrication approach that combines the benefits of extrusion and stacking, which is capable of realising high-nonlinearity lead-silicate glass holey fibers with tailorable dispersion characteristics. We also present optimised fiber designs offering dispersion-shifted and flattened performance at 1.55 mum

articleTitle: Inhibiting pattern-effects in semiconductor optical amplifier using carrier reservoir in an asymmetrical multiple quantum well structure
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose an asymmetric quantum well semiconductor optical amplifier in which the wider bandgap quantum wells act as carrier-reservoirs replenishing carriers in narrower quantum wells of the active region. 10 Gbps pattern-effect free gain was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Spatial reuse on the optical burst transport network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical burst transport (OBT), a novel WDM ring network, is a promising contender for the new metropolitan area network. In this paper, we investigate the spatial reuse property of the OBT, which is able to significantly improve the network performance.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependent channel performance in long haul WDM systems and its usage in all optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In long haul WDM-systems the reach of the individual channels depends on the wavelength. In all optical networks this can be used to avoid regeneration if an appropriate wavelength assignment is applied. Network case studies support the according simulation results.

articleTitle: Tunable Er/sup 3+//Yb/sup 3+/ codoped fiber amplifiers covering S- and C-Bands (1460 /spl sim/ 1580 nm) based on discrete fundamental modecutoff
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate thermo-optic wavelength-tunable Er/sup 3+/TYb/sup 3+/ co-doped fiber amplifiers by using discrete in-line tunable short-pass tapered-fiber filters based on tunable material dispersion. The amplification can occur from 1460 nm to 1580 nm, covering both the S- and C- bands.

articleTitle: WiMAX services over transport networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The merging of long-haul carriers with wireless operators signals significant changes in telecommunications services in the US. Wireless access is likely to become ubiquitous, while efficient fiber based transport provides the necessary bandwidth for aggregated traffic transport. Recently, WiMAX wireless technology had been tried out in places across the world. WiMAX technology promises a quick and cheap deployment of broadband and voice services over a non-line-of-sight wireless channel. In addition, WiMax radios probe the air channel so as to dynamically adapt to atmospheric conditions. This paper addresses the provisioning of voice and data services over a combined WiMAX/optical network. We address issues such as wireless channel call blocking of voice services and transport bandwidth provisioning schemes vis-a-vis packet loss performance of a wireless/transport network.

articleTitle: Investigation of fiber based gates for time division demultiplexing up to 640 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally investigate the switching performance of interferometric gates based on highly nonlinear fiber (HNLF), a Kerr-gate and a nonlinear optical loop mirror. Switching windows are measured and compared for different operation conditions and HNLFs

articleTitle: Compact optical pulse compressor based on comb-like profiled fiber comprised of HNLF and hole-assisted fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We develop a hole-assisted fiber with large anomalous dispersion and low macro-bending loss to realize compact module of CPF pulse compressor. Using the fabricated module, we demonstrate C-band wavelength-tunable pulse compression for 40 GHz pulse train

articleTitle: A novel flat-band long period grating with special apodization induced by high frequency CO/sub 2/ laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a special modulation of refractive index design for obtaining long period fiber grating (LPFG) with a broad-band and top flattened transmission spectrum. The LPFG with modulation envelope of refractive index like Gaussian function was fabricated by high frequency CO/sub 2/ laser pulses in this paper, and the experimental results showed that the top rejection bandwidth was up to 10 nm and the top flatness was less than 0.5 dB, which will have potential applications in optical communications, such as polarization-dependent loss compensators, band selection filters, course wavelength division multiplexers and so on.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s transmission over 3 km at 850 nm using single-mode photonic crystal fiber, single-mode VCSEL, and Si-APD
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated 10 Gb/s, 3 km transmission at 850 nm using a single-mode photonic crystal fiber (PCF), a VCSEL, and a Si-avalanche photodiode. 10 Gb/s NRZ signals were successfully transmitted over a 3 km-long PCF.

articleTitle: 11.4 dB isolation on an amplifying AlGaInAs/InP optical waveguide isolator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 11.4 dB optical isolation combined with forward transparency is demonstrated on a TM-mode amplifying AlGaInAs/InP optical waveguide isolator operating at 1300 nm. Basis for this isolator configuration is non-reciprocal absorption caused by the magneto-optic Kerr effect.

articleTitle: Differential mode delay analysis for a multimode optical fiber with Fourier-domain low-coherence interferometry
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel differential mode delay (DMD) measurement for a multimode optical fiber using the Fourier-domain low-coherence interferometry (fLCI) for the first time has been proposed. Our experimental results have a good agreement with those results obtained using a conventional method

articleTitle: Optical intensity discriminator based on strongly enhanced ellipse rotation in circular-birefringence fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel type of optical intensity discriminator based on the ellipse rotation in a highly twisted circular-birefringence fiber. The applicability to a simple and stable all-optical 2R regenerator is demonstrated at 40 Gbit/s

articleTitle: A novel PolSK transceiver based on differential demodulation: assessment of performance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present simulation and experimental results on PolSK modulation based on simple transmitter and receiver setups, using, for the first time to our knowledge, a differential demodulation based on the asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer.

articleTitle: Virtual distributed Gires-Tournois etalon based on phase-modulated wideband chirped fiber grating
