publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we propose and demonstrate a novel virtual Gires-Tournois etalon, which is realized by introducing phase-modulation in a linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating. Such etalons can be used as dispersion compensation devices in optical transmission systems.

articleTitle: Huge birefringence in couplers made of microfibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We herein present simulation and experimental results that demonstrate the importance of polarization effects in couplers and devices made of microfibers, i.e. fibers having wavelength scale diameters. We derive the consequences for loop microresonators.

articleTitle: All-fiber electrooptical polarization control
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical fibers gain a second order nonlinearity through thermal poling. The voltage induced birefringence is small. An all-fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer was then constructed enabling electrooptical polarization control with 78 V and sub-microsecond response time.

articleTitle: Ultra low power consumption silica-based PLC switch using tapered narrow ridge structures
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We achieved a silica based PLC thermo-optic switch with a power consumption only 30 mW without any deterioration in the optical properties by using tapered narrow ridge structures.

articleTitle: Ethernet in the other first mile: North American case studies for IEEE 802.3ah in applications beyond FTTH
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The proliferation of FTTH is impacting the cost of components, driving the development of new standards, and influencing installation practices. Likewise, the ratification of IEEE 802.3ah and its adoption by carriers has engendered the creation of cost-effective, scalable, and highly manageable devices for the delivery of Ethernet over fiber. This paper establishes the context for IEEE 802.3ah by examining some large scale deployments in Japan's FTTH market, and then focuses on examining why similar technologies have been deployed in much smaller, non-carrier applications in North America.

articleTitle: 1 b/s/Hz coherent WDM transmission over 112 km of dispersion managed optical fibre
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The performance advantage of using dispersion-managed fibre in coherent WDM systems is demonstrated. Limitations due to nonlinearity are no more severe for a 298 Gb/s coherent WDM signal than for an individual 42.6 Gb/s channel.

articleTitle: First demonstration of a polarization insensitive low time jitter and optical noise tolerant all-optical clock recovery at 40 GHz using a self-pulsating laser tandem
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a polarization insensitive all-optical clock recovery, tolerant for an input optical signal to noise ratio as low as 15dB/0.1 nm, by cascading a bulk-based and a quantum-dots based self-pulsating lasers at 4OGbit/s.

articleTitle: Efficient nonlinearity cancellation through optical phase conjugation into an embedded link with asymmetrical power profiles
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate, for the first time, that nonlinearity compensation into an embedded link with strongly asymmetrical power profiles can be obtained using a properly modified phase conjugation setup

articleTitle: Novel demultiplexer for ultra high speed pulses using a perfect phase-matched parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel transparent demultiplexer for ultra fast pulse trains using a 19 m long HNLF-based parametric amplifier is proposed. Using this multiplexer, 320-10 Gb/s OTDM DEMUX with parametric gains over 20 dB were successfully implemented

articleTitle: A novel parallel scheduling protocol based on JET in optical burst switching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel signaling protocol called PS-JET for avoiding extra ETE delay in JET/OBS is proposed. It completes the resource reservation by two steps, and shows great improvement on the reduction of ETE delay compared with PJET

articleTitle: Short optical pulse generator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We developed the short optical pulse generator with function of wavelength sweeping (SPG) which can generate TL pulse train under the condition of wavelength sweep range from 1550 nm to 1560 nm with sweeping step of 1 nm and dwell time of 5 s. We demonstrated chromatic dispersion measurement of EDFA by time of flight method for a short time of 55 s using SPG

articleTitle: Supercontinuum and gas cell in a single microstructured fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We exploit both the high nonlinearity and holey structure of microstructured fibers to combine an ultra-broadband light source and a gas cell in a single microstructured fiber filled with acetylene.

articleTitle: Ultra-wide-band low loss and PDL 1/spl times/32 splitter polymer optical waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We fabricated 1 /spl times/ 32 splitter device based on Si substrate using spin perfluorinated polymer. We could demonstrate 1 /spl times/ 32 splitter device of low loss and PDL in ultra-wide-band range (1.31 /spl mu/m/1.55/1.65 /spl mu/m).

articleTitle: Error-free 31-hop cascaded operation of an optical packet switching router with all-optical 3R regeneration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper demonstrates 31-hop cascaded operation of an optical-label switching router. The all-optical 3R regeneration enables error-free 31-hop cascaded packet switching with no additional penalty beyond 3 hops up to 31 hops.

articleTitle: 1.25 Gb/s uplink burst-mode transmissions: system requirements and optical diagnostic challenges of EPON physical-layer chipset for enabling broadband optical Ethernet access networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents new physical-layer chipset to achieve high-performance uplink burst-mode transmissions for 1.25 Gb/s Ethernet PON (EPON). System requirements and optical diagnostic challenges are discussed with system performance demonstrated exceeding the specifications defined in IEEE 802.3ah standards.

articleTitle: Optical 3R regeneration using a clock-modulated pump and higher-order four-wave mixing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In the 3R signal, the use of a clock-modulated pump reduced timing jitter by up to 5.8 ps and reduced inter-symbol interference. Receiver sensitivity improvements of up to 5.0 dB and 10.9 dB were also obtained for signals degraded by ASE noise and dispersion, respectively

articleTitle: Waveband burst switching - a new approach to networking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a waveband grooming strategy for optical burst switching. We show that by grouping bursts into wavebands, a large reduction in network equipment costs can be effected. This makes burst switching attractive for use in high capacity core networks.

articleTitle: Electronic dispersion compensation for enhanced optical transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Summary form only for tutorial. Electronic dispersion compensation by analog and digital equalizers enable a considerable increase of high bit rate optical transmission system tolerances. Electronic equalizers are small size and low power consumption subsystems suitable for compact transponder integration.

articleTitle: Variable sized packet routing in a complete 12/spl times/12 photonic network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Packets with variable sized payloads between 96 and 384 bytes, depending upon the number of payload wavelengths, are simultaneously routed in an implemented 12/spl times/12 optical packet switching network with bit error rates better than 10/sup -12/.

articleTitle: All-optical high speed NOR gate based on two photon absorption in silicon wire waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time an all-optical logic NOR gate in submicron size silicon wire waveguides. High speed operation at equivalent 80 Gbps data rate was achieved using pump induced non-degenerate two-photon absorption inside the waveguides. The device requires low pulse energy (few pJ) for logic gate operation

articleTitle: An all-fiber low-noise hybrid erbium-Brillouin amplified laser source
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel all-fiber hybrid erbium-Brillouin amplified laser source, and achieve 8-dB reduction of RIN compared with an EDFA based source. The resulting spurious-free dynamic range in an analog system is improved by 6.8 dB

articleTitle: Data-polarization-insensitive wavelength conversion in a PPLN waveguide by cross-polarization-modulation of the pump using an SOA
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel method of wavelength-conversion in a PPLN-waveguide using polarization-modulation of its pump. Polarization-insensitive, all-optical, intensity-to-polarization conversion in an SOA is used to reduce the PPLN waveguide's polarization-sensitivity from >30 dB to <1 dB

articleTitle: Recent advances on laser processing in silica-based PLCs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Laser processing is a powerful tool for realizing highly functional silica-based PLCs that can provide simple methods for tuning device characteristics and enhance new functionalities. This letter reviews laser processing technologies for silica-based PLCs. Furthermore, this letter describes flat-top AWG spectrum tilt compensation and three-dimensional waveguide interconnection using laser processing

articleTitle: Unique all-fiber tunable filter using a single resonant-band LPG and nanoparticle dispersed electro-optic polymer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A single resonant band, thin cladding long-period grating (LPG) is tuned using a nanoparticle dispersed electro-optic polymer. The LPG has been tuned over 10 nm and has a potential tuning range upwards of 50 nm.

articleTitle: Hybrid integrated electrooptic polymeric digital optical switches (DOS's) with lower loss
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simply structured hybrid integrated electrooptic polymeric digital optical switch is proposed and demonstrated. The loss of the devices is improved by integration of passive material with switching properties similar to switches without passive material.

articleTitle: Radio-over-fiber distribution system with OEO repeater for 3G cellular systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have proposed a new radio-over-fiber (ROF) distribution system for 3G cellular systems, which can concentrate ROF signals from distributed cells on one optical fiber deployed on existing optical access systems, and have successfully demonstrated sufficient reverse-link communications.

articleTitle: Effects of cumulative PDG on the scalability of SOA-based optical packet switching networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using a re-circulating loop we study the extreme cases of cumulative PDG in SOA-based packet switching nodes. We show that node polarization dependence could limit the physical layer scalability of optical packet switching networks.

articleTitle: Realistic designs of silica hollow-core bandgap fibers free of surface
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By systematically studying feasible silica PBGFs core structures we identify new designs regimes that robustly eliminate the presence of surface modes. New realistic fibers designs with a fundamental mode free of anticrossings at all frequencies within the bandgap are proposed

articleTitle: Software solution to decrease RSVP-TE signaling processing time in ASON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The GMPLS RSVP-TE signaling protocol is widely used in intelligent optical networks. Faster signaling processing time provides shorter time of resource on demand and restoration for failure. This paper proposes a software solution with the planar-chain approach (PCA), which utilizes the planar-chain data storage structure in the state block of RSVP-TE to reduce the signaling processing time complexity from O(N/sup 2/) to O(N). Numerical results demonstrate that the PCA is much faster than the traditional linear-chain approach (LCA).

articleTitle: Microstructured and multicore fibers and fiber lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Microstructured and multi-core fiber lasers were fabricated that have produced more than 1.3 W/cm at 1.5 mum. Near 2 W single frequency, single-transverse-mode output was demonstrated

articleTitle: Fabrication and investigation of fast response variable optical attenuator on silica substrate
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have developed fast response variable optical attenuator (VOA) on silica substrate by analyzing thermal response using equivalent circuit. The response time and power consumption are 2.5 msec and 100 mW respectively

articleTitle: Volume manufacturing and deployment of large-scale photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Manufacturing statistics are presented for 100 Gb/s transmitter and receiver large-scale photonic integrated circuits (LS-PICs). The data demonstrate the feasibility of the cost-effective deployment and volume manufacturing of these devices

articleTitle: 40 Gbit/s packet-wavelength-selective, reconfigurable optical add/drop multiplexing using label-selectivity-enhanced optical en/decoder and wide-passband AOTF
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the packet-wavelength-selective reconfigurable OADM network on 16-wavelength /spl times/ 40-Gbit/s NRZ signal using a label-selectivity-enhanced optical en/decoder and wide-passband AOTF. Error-free operations for all 16-wavelength channels at three nodes with 100-km transmission are realized.

articleTitle: Slow light in bulk materials and optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This study investigates slow light in bulk materials and optical fibers. Progress in developing new slow-light techniques and applications are also presented. Slow light techniques hold great promise for applications in telecom and quantum information processing

articleTitle: Novel spacing-tunable multiwavelength Raman fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a multiwavelength Raman fiber laser with a continuously tunable spacing and an independently adjustable channel number. Spacing tuning from 0.3 to 0.6 nm and channel number adjustment from 2 to 10 have been achieved

articleTitle: Design of microstructured single-mode fiber combining large mode area and high rare earth ion concentration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new design of microstructured fiber combining large and highly doped area, low bend loss and single-mode propagation. An original guiding regime is governed by characteristics of high index cladding rods.

articleTitle: A broadcast and multicast-enabled switch architecture utilizing a gateless channel selection scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a new switch architecture that supports simultaneous multicasting/broadcasting for all input ports. Unlike existing architectures, it does not require any optical ON-OFF gates, and is transparent to signal modulation format and bit-rate.

articleTitle: Loss and bandgap analysis in air-core photonic bandgap fiber for IR transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show that loss is minimized at an air-filling factor of 0.8 with a refractive index of 2.4 in photonic bandgap chalcogenide fiber (lambda = 4 mum). This air-filling factor also corresponds to the maximum relative bandgap

articleTitle: Novel control methods to enlarge dispersion range of tunable dispersion compensator using angled etalons with multiple reflections
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose some novel control methods for 40-Gbps etalon based tunable dispersion compensators. We developed two compensators; one with a low 3.2-dB loss (no circulator required) and the one with a wide 620 ps/nm tunable range

articleTitle: Coating damage suppression in hole-assisted fiber for high optical power wiring
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Effective suppression of temperature increase (< 1 K, at 3 W) was observed in hole-assisted fiber (HAF) with tight bending. We report for the first time suppression due to reduction of whispering gallery mode and HAF's applicability at 100 W

articleTitle: Optimum modulation format for high density and/or long haul transmission at 40 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We will review some promising modulation formats that have been proposed in the past years to improve either the information spectral density and/or the achievable transmission distance of 40 Gb/s systems

articleTitle: Faraday Effect in Long Telecom Fibers with Randomly Varying Birefringence
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We measure relative propagation delay between two orthogonally polarized pulses in long fibers in the presence of a weak axial magnetic field (~50μT). We find that the fiber birefringence modifies the Faraday polarization eigenstates, which became noncircular and wander in time.

articleTitle: Fabrication of 1D and 2D grating structures
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an interferometric method of fabricating 1-dimensional and 2-dimensional periodic structures on planar substrates. There is no limitation on the grating length and the technique is applicable to fabrication of fiber Bragg gratings

articleTitle: Laser cleaving of optical connectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: From single mode to multimode, simplex to multifiber, all connector termination processes require the excess fiber to be cleaved and "denubbed" and the residual epoxy (bead) to be removed prior to the polishing operation. While accepted as the industry's standard practice, mechanical hand scribing, or "nick and pull" techniques, are often the source of poor endface quality and low yields, resulting in high manufacturing costs and questionable long-term reliability. Mechanical hand scribing techniques are particularly susceptible to operator-dependent variability, tool-dependent variability, and uncontrollable stress propagation inherent to the glass. Fiber optic connector manufacturers have long searched for alternative cleaving technologies that would mitigate the undesirable effects of mechanical hand scribing. Laser cleaving technology, though historically perceived as a costly and accessibly limited option, is rapidly gaining acceptance as a viable alternative to mechanical hand scribing. This paper investigates the physics and reliability of laser cleaving. We will also explore the practical advantages, including economic benefits, of manufacturing using laser cleaving technologies.

articleTitle: The power of dispersion management for 10-Gb/s and 40-Gb/s systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review applications and requirements of dispersion compensation that enable high-capacity, long-haul, and ultra-long-haul 10-Gb/s and 40-Gb/s DWDM transmission. We briefly describe their impact on system performance and present some future perspectives.

articleTitle: Application of the Magnus expansion to polarization mode dispersion and polarization dependent loss
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We solve the differential equation for the frequency-dependent Mueller matrix for systems affected by both of PMD and PDL with a Magnus expansion approach. The formalism is then applied to compensator design

articleTitle: Magneto-photonic crystal slab waveguides with lower-refractive-index claddings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Magneto-photonic crystal slab waveguides which include nanoporous SiO/sub 2/ with a very low refractive index as the cladding material, exhibit low losses and high nonreciprocal phase shifts without the need for holes extended to the claddings.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a simple time-of-flight rangefinder based on semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a unique design of a time-of-flight laser ranger that detects the distance and reflectivity of a target based on cross-gain modulation between counter-propagating pulses in a semiconductor optical amplifier, without using high-speed electronics

articleTitle: Linear frequency resolved optical gating as a line monitoring tool
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the use of spectrograms for pulse monitoring. The technique can characterize the phase and intensity of data modulated pulses after transmission over a fiber span including a tunable dispersion compensating grating

articleTitle: Demonstration of 28 GHz ring resonator based electro-optic polymer modulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a ring resonator based traveling wave electro-optic polymer modulator. Efficient modulation at 28 GHz (FSR of the resonator) with 3 dBe bandwidth of 7 GHz is achieved.

articleTitle: Novel NRZ-to-RZ format conversion with tunable pulsewidth using phase modulator and interleaver
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a 10-Gb/s NRZ-to-RZ format conversion with tunable pulsewidth using phase modulation followed by interleaver. RZ signals with pulsewidth of 34-84 ps are obtained with extinction ratio over 15 dB and negative power penalty.

articleTitle: Chirp managed laser (CML): A compact transmitter for dispersion tolerant 10 Gb/s networking applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show that the compact combination of a directly modulated laser and an optical filter, generates a highly dispersion tolerant modulation format suitable for > 200 km reach at 10 Gbps without dispersion compensation

articleTitle: Programmable, polarization-independent, and DWDM-chromatic dispersion compensator using a virtually-imaged phased-array and spatial light modulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a programmable, polarization-independent, and DWDM-capable chromatic dispersion compensator based on a virtually-imaged phased-array and spatial light modulator providing both positive and negative dispersion with tuning range of -2040 /spl sim/ +850 ps/nm.

articleTitle: Link dimensioning in burst switching-based optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a link dimensioning issue in burst switching-based optical networks. The optimal number of wavelengths in a link pursuing the lowest burst blocking is obtained by taking into account the effect of the transport and the control plane.

articleTitle: WDM OFM-based radio-over-fiber distribution antenna system employing GCSR tunable lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally the feasibility of a wavelength-multiplexed radio-over-fiber distribution antenna system in a star-tree configuration based on optical frequency multiplication and employing GCSR tunable lasers for the generation of the swept light source.

articleTitle: A survivable WDM PON with alternate-path switching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a survivable WDM PON with simple ONUs. By employing our proposed alternate-path switching scheme, traffic can be restored promptly under feeder and distribution fiber link failures as well as the AWG failure in the RN simultaneously.

articleTitle: Hollow waveguide distributed Bragg reflector for widely tunable optical devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a tunable hollow waveguide Bragg reflector for widely tunable optical devices, exhibiting a narrow-pass-band filter and tunable laser using the tunable reflector. Also, the integration of a MEMS thermal actuator was demonstrated for the first time.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated widely tunable delayed interference based 40 Gbps wavelength converter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 40 Gbps operation of a novel monolithically integrated wavelength converter consisting of a sampled grating DBR laser, long SOA and a delay interferometer (DI)-MZI is reported. Chip performance is studied in detail as function of output filter bandwidth and detuning.

articleTitle: PMD characterization of installed fiber networks - compromise between result accuracy and measurement time
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: FiberWork has conducted PMD field characterization in over 500,000 km of installed fibers. Such extensive database has been used to derive the minimum measuring time required to provide acceptable PMD measurement accuracies. The analysis is presented in this paper and is done in terms of PMD levels and fiber plant types. Useful orientations for optimizing PMD field characterization and lower its costs while keeping acceptable results are discussed.

articleTitle: Tunable add/drop filter for CWDM system using cladding mode coupling assisted by long-period fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a tunable fiber add/drop filter suitable for coarse wavelength division multiplexing (CWDM) systems. The light coupling between two fibers was performed through the cladding modes assisted by two identical long-period fiber gratings (LPGs). Experimentally, 75% net coupling efficiency was achieved and the side lobes were suppressed by -24 dB.

articleTitle: Yb-doped amplifier fiber with distributed filtering by resonant core-ring coupling
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An Yb-doped amplifier fiber with distributed gain filtering along its length was fabricated. Measured amplified spontaneous emission confirms gain suppression at wavelengths relevant to important laser noise components. Pump efficiency improvement was observed.

articleTitle: Brillouin scattering in optical fibers for high resolution wavelength and line width measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a simple method for measuring the wavelength and line width of optical sources with a resolution in the femtometer range. This method is based on the small bandwidth of Brillouin scattering

articleTitle: Continuous-wave supercontinuum generation from an erbium-doped fiber ring laser incorporating a highly nonlinear optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate a simple and novel erbium-doped fiber based continuous-wave supercontinuum laser. High quality of depolarized supercontinuum output with a bandwidth larger than 200 nm is achieved with a ring cavity incorporating a 2-km highly nonlinear fiber.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of slow light via four-wave mixing in semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally the generation of slow light at room temperature via four-wave mixing in SOAs. Tunable delays up to 913 ps was obtained at 0.5 GHz, corresponding to a record delay-bandwidth product of 0.46.

articleTitle: Design of gain-flattened highly nonlinear photonic crystal fiber Raman amplifier using a single pump: a leakage loss approach
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a novel inherent gain-flattened design of highly nonlinear photonic crystal fiber Raman amplifier exhibiting /spl plusmn/0.85-dB gain-ripples over 28-nm bandwidth using a single pump in C-band employing the leakage loss property with integrated dispersion compensation functionality.

articleTitle: Rapidly reconfigurable phase code generation and recognition using fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 16-chip, 40 Gchip/s, reconfigurable fiber Bragg grating based quaternary phase en/decoder with a tuning time of <2s between two different phase codes.

articleTitle: Highly birefringent long period gratings fabricated with femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Long period gratings (LPG) in standard fiber have been manufactured with a sharply focused near infrared (NIR) femtosecond laser beam. Polarization splitting of the attenuation bands is strongly dependent upon the inscription power.

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical devices based on carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Various nonlinear optical devices based on carbon nanotube-polyimide saturable absorber are demonstrated. Thin film mode-lockers can achieve 165 fs for Er fiber laser and 68 fs for Er/Yb glass laser. Microcavity and waveguide structures can be fabricated.

articleTitle: A novel provisioning framework for dual-node interconnected SONET/SDH rings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a new approach to provision connections in a network of dual-node interconnected rings. Our approach satisfies the unique constraints imposed by SONET/SDH standards and is very useful for reducing link capacity fragmentation.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated 1/spl times/32 optical splitter/router low loss ripple MZI-based WDM filter and low loss Y-branch circuit
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a novel monolithically integrated 1/spl times/32 optical splitter/router with functions as an optical splitter for 1.31 /spl mu/m-band, 1.49 /spl mu/m-band and as a wavelength router for 1.55 /spl mu/m-band using a low loss ripple MZI-based WDM filter and a low loss Y-branch circuit.

articleTitle: Need-oriented waveguide design based on wavefront matching method
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The wavefront matching method provides us with a new way to obtain the optimum shape for waveguides used in planar lightwave circuit devices. This presentation reviews the principle behind the method and shows its usefulness with some experimental results.

articleTitle: TM mode optical waveguide isolator with 8.8 dB/mm nonreciprocal propagation induced by ferromagnetic MnAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 1540 nm, TM mode waveguide isolator based on the nonreciprocal loss shift was developed. It consisted of a semiconductor waveguide with a ferromagnetic MnAs layer and showed an isolation ratio of 8.8 dB/mm

articleTitle: Widely wavelength-tunable femtosecond pulse generation based on comb-like profiled fiber comprised of HNLF and zero dispersion-slope NZDSF
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using a dispersion-flattened comb-like profiled fiber comprised of HNLF and zero dispersion-slope NZDSF, we demonstrate extremely wideband wavelength-tunable femtosecond pulse generation. 100-fs optical pulses are successfully generated for the wavelengths of 1530, 1570, and 1610nm.

articleTitle: A new efficient online-optimization approach for SDH/SONET-WDM multi layer networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents and evaluates a new simple greedy algorithm for rerouting connections in a dynamic SDH/SONET-WDM multi layer network to improve resource efficiency and thus increase network performance.

articleTitle: Planar lightwave circuits for PON applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Many components used in passive optical networks (PONs) can be fabricated on a planar lightwave circuit (PLC). These include 1/spl times/N splitters, 2/spl times/N splitters and video overlay filters. A broadband 2/spl times/2 splitter is a critical component for PON. A directional coupler and even a single stage Mach-Zehnder is unsuitable for this application because each provides a splitting ratio that has excessive wavelength dependence. We demonstrate a PLC-based, broadband 2/spl times/2 splitter constructed from a two-stage lattice filter that has low loss and high uniformity from 1260 nm to 1625 nm. Y-branch splitters can be cascaded to make 1/spl times/N splitters or integrated with a 2/spl times/2 splitter to make 2/spl times/N splitters. We compare insertion loss and uniformity for splitters that are fabricated with silica on silicon technology versus silica on quartz technology. By using silica on quartz technology, we demonstrate low-loss 1/spl times/32 splitters. The 2/spl times/32 splitter has increased functionality with negligible loss penalty. We demonstrate that PLC-based splitters satisfy all reliability requirements. A video overlay filter can be used for video overlay onto a bidirectional, digital, fiber optic communication system. The video overlay uses 1550 nm light, while the digital communication system either uses 1310 nm light in both directions or uses 1310 nm light for one direction and 1490 nm light in the other direction. With PLC technology, the filter is based on integrated Mach-Zehnders. We also demonstrate a video overlay filter designed for digital channels using both 1310 nm light and 1490 nm light.

articleTitle: The First Application-driven Lambda-on-Demand Field Trial over a US Nationwide Network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The Lambda-on-demand functionality with link aggregation to accommodate the dynamic bandwidth demands of an ultra-high-resolution visualization application was realized in over a US nationwide photonic network for the first time.

articleTitle: DSP-based oscillator technology greatly simplifies timing architectures in multi-service platforms
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Networking equipment must support a diverse and growing set of data rates including 10 G Ethernet, 10 G fibre channel, SONET OC-192 and the associated forward error correction (EEC) rates. Traditional timing sub-system architectures use a single crystal or SAW resonator for each frequency resulting in a plethora of individual oscillators on each port card. By using a DSP-based clock synthesis IC, multiple output frequencies can be generated from a single, low-frequency crystal resonator. Integrating the clock synthesis IC with the low-frequency quartz crystal into a hermetic ceramic package enables the development of multiple frequency crystal oscillator (XO) and voltage-controlled crystal oscillator (VCXO) devices. Key specifications, such as frequency stability, long-term aging, drift and mechanical integrity, are significantly improved over high-frequency fundamental (HFF) crystals or SAW-based oscillators.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Ethernet OAM functionality for management of layer 2 switches connected to the resilient packet ring equipment in the metro area networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate standard based Ethernet operation administration and maintenance (OAM) functionalities by the Ethernet OAM frame in the Ethernet network based on the resilient packet ring (RPR) based architecture. This paper describes the requirements for highly reliable Ethernet services in the metro area network from the operator's point of view. The Ethernet continuity check and the Ethernet loop back functionalities in the RPR based Ethernet network with several scenarios that may exist in the commercial operation are successfully confirmed for the first time.

articleTitle: High nonlinearity bismuth fibers and their applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based optical fiber which exhibits an extra-high nonlinear optical coefficient is developed. Linear and nonlinear optical properties of Bi2O3-based optical fiber is discussed. Loss management and applications of the fiber are also reported

articleTitle: Optical ring services in GMPLS based mesh networks: an implementation of optical GRID
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A smart and flexible distributed optical network control scheme in GMPLS based mesh networks is presented and implemented for the optical ring topology network services which support large-scale distributed computing applications such as GRID computing.

articleTitle: Optical tunable asymmetric interleaver
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel optical tunable asymmetric interleaver is demonstrated. It consists of two symmetric interleaves with wavelength shifting capability in series. It can deliver continuous tunable interleaving ratios for WDM applications, particularly for 10 G+40 G network upgrade.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity enhancement of filled microstructured fibers operating in the nanowire regime
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We predict significant enhancement of the effective nonlinear coefficient of soft glass nanowires and nanostructured fibers by surrounding the cores with a nonlinear liquid. Using bismuth nanostructured fibers, /spl gamma/ as high as 3900 W/sup -1/km/sup -1/ is possible.

articleTitle: Triple play services over a converged optical/wireless network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper introduces a high performance architecture to demonstrate a triple play services delivery over optical/wireless converged networks. Applications including VoD (video on demand), VoIP and IPTV have been added to the emulated converged network.

articleTitle: An efficient scheduling scheme for on-demand lightpath reservations in reconfigurable WDM optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose an efficient scheduling scheme that optimizes advance-reserved lightpath services in reconfigurable WDM networks. A re-optimization approach is devised to reallocate network resources for dynamic service demands while keeping determined schedule unchanged.

articleTitle: 30 Gb/s transmission over 40 km directly modulated DFB laser-based SMF links without optical amplification and dispersion compensation for VSR and metro applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: It is shown that 30 Gb/s transmission over 40 km standard fibre of adaptively modulated optical OFDM signals is feasible for directly modulated DFB laser-based links without optical amplification and dispersion compensation. The corresponding loss margin is >4 dB.

articleTitle: The lowest-loss of 0.35 dB/km in an aluminum-doped SM optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the lowest attenuation of 0.35 dB/km @ 1550 nm achieved in the aluminum-doped, SMF-28reg-like, SM optical fiber. Additional features such as lower n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, dispersion, and dispersion-slope, higher SBS threshold and better profiling stability have also been demonstrated

articleTitle: Low Drive Voltage, Negative Chirp 40 Gb/s EA-Modulator/Widely-Tunable Laser Transmitter, Using Quantum-Well-Intermixing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present the first 40Gb/s widely-tunable EAM/laser transmitters demonstrating 1.0-1.5V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PtoP</inf>drive, low-chirp, and under 0.5dB of power penalty for transmission through 2.3km of fiber. A robust quantum-well-intermixing technique was employed for the realization of these devices.

articleTitle: Digital implementation of soft detection for 3-chip-DBPSK with improved receiver sensitivity and dispersion tolerance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a digital implementation of soft detection for 3-chip differential binary phase-shift keying with improved receiver sensitivity and tolerance to chromatic dispersion. An optimum weighting factor is found for signals degraded by correlated phase distortions resulting from chromatic dispersion.

articleTitle: Advances in SiGe ICs for 40 Gb/s signal equalization
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: IC technologies and major equalizer structures were discussed for designing a 40 Gb/s equalizer chip. Insights, suggestions or comments were given on designing all building blocks for an equalizer circuit, design methodology, and packaging the die.

articleTitle: Optical networking testbeds in Europe
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This talk will present an update on the status of optical networking test-beds and the large scale utilisation of photonic communications systems by the research community in Europe.

articleTitle: Low loss and highly reliable polymer optical waveguides with perfluorinated dopant-free core
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Polarization independent and low propagation loss of 0.03 dB/cm even at 1650 nm was obtained by the polymer optical waveguide with the dopant-free core made of purely perfluorinated amorphous polymer. High durability to humidity was also shown

articleTitle: Demonstration of a complete and fully functional end-to-end asynchronous optical packet switched network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A fully functional optical packet switched network able to transport variable length and asynchronous optical packets is demonstrated. This includes packet switching, label recognition and rewriting, fast laser tuning, wavelength conversion, optical packet transceiver functionality.

articleTitle: Optical VPN in PON Using TDM-FDM signal format
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a simple and low-cost PON with optical VPN functionality using a directly modulated laser diode to generate TDM-FDM format. This format enables that one tributary of the transmitted signal be reflected to ONUs in the same optical VPN.

articleTitle: First demonstration of synchronization-free nanosecond label switching node utilizing 1/spl times/8 PLZT switch
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel synchronization-free label switching with latency as small as 300 nanoseconds utilizing 1/spl times/8 PLZT switch was demonstrated for the first time. Autonomous multi-hop switching experiment in a tree network cascading three nodes was also successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Phase-preservation capability of all-optical amplitude regenerators using fiber nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Phase preservation by all-optical amplitude regenerators using fiber nonlinearity is experimentally examined. It is shown that regenerators based on soliton filtering or on saturation of FWM interaction induce less phase fluctuations than that based on spectrum broadening and slicing.

articleTitle: Insights on delivering an IP triple play over GE-PON and GPON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Insights on delivering an IP triple play over GE-PON and GPON. This paper looks at the methods and technologies for delivering voice, video and data IP services over PON networks.

articleTitle: A novel perturbation method for signal-noise interaction in nonlinear dispersive fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel perturbation method for signal-noise interaction in nonlinear dispersive fibers is presented. It is simple and more accurate than the regular perturbation method, and is suitable for system performance analysis

articleTitle: 511-chip SSFBG and DFG-based optical thresholder enabled compound data rate (10 Gbps/spl sim/622 Mbps) OCDMA experiment for multiple service provisioning platform
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a compound data rate (10 Gbps /spl sim/ 622 Mbps) OCDMA system for the future multiple service provisioning on demand. This achievement was due to record-long 511-chip SSFBG and DFG-based optical thresholder to reduce MAI and ISI noises.

articleTitle: 80+ GBit/s ETDM systems implementation: an overview of current technologies
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This presentation will show recent advances in the fields of ultra-high speed micro-electronic and electro-optic component technologies has made possible the implementation and successfully demonstration of experimental ETDM-based optical transmission systems at bit rates in excess of 80 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of SBC's "fiber to the node" network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The FTTN/FTTP strategy delivers an optimal balance of network capability, cost, speed of deployment, reliability and convenience for customers. Reliability is one of the key aspects of this new architecture, especially since it delivers delay-sensitive voice and video services in addition to data services. This paper provides the results of the most recent FTTN network reliability studies conducted by SBC. These studies include availability/downtime analysis of various segments of the network, from the residential gateway to the fiber nodes in the neighborhood as well as the network equipment in the central offices and video hub offices. The paper also addresses layer 1 and layer 2/3 restoration and protection mechanisms as they apply to the FTTN network, and it compares applicable protocols (1+1 & M:N redundancies, MPLS, VRRP, etc.) in light of the services they are protecting and the customer impact they have. The paper presents the diversity and availability options for various segments relative to each other, showing how the access network has a major impact on the reliability, while illustrating the stringent requirement for the backbone video network.

articleTitle: Near-single sideband modulation in strong optical injection-locked semiconductor lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Asymmetric modulation sidebands have been demonstrated by controlling frequency detuning of strong optical injection-locked semiconductor lasers. Near-single sideband generated by the technique significantly reduces fiber chromatic-dispersion effect with enhanced modulation bandwidth.

articleTitle: Performance of NRZ and duobinary modulation formats in Rayleigh and ASE-dominated dense optical links
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The performance of spectrally compressed optical modulation formats in the presence of Rayleigh and ASE-dominated noise are investigated and quantified. The results show that wider modulation formats outperform narrower bandwidth formats unless format-tailored filtering is used.

articleTitle: A novel robust OSNR monitoring technique with 40-dB dynamic range using phase modulator embedded fiber loop mirror
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel in-band OSNR monitoring technique using phase modulator embedded fiber loop mirror (PM-FLM) is proposed and demonstrated. Monitoring error can be kept <0.25 dB for OSNR between 0 to 40 dB in 10-Gb/s non-return-to-zero (NRZ) system.

articleTitle: 375 THz Parametric Translation of Modulated Signal from 1550nm to Visible Band
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Record parametric frequency-translation of NRZ-modulated signal over 375THz is demonstrated using silica-PCF. The 1550-nm band is mapped to visible 500-nm spectral window, proving the feasibility of all-fiber universal band translator. Both single-channel and WDM architectures are constructed and demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Dimensioning of active broadcast channels in access IPTV network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The number of active broadcast TV channels between central office and access node and its sensitivity to channel popularity distribution and to the number of set top boxes simultaneously tuned to broadcast channels is investigated.

articleTitle: Calculation of the bit-error ratio in wavelength-division-multiplexed return-to-zero systems when the nonlinear penalty is dominated collision-induced timing jitter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze the accuracy of a simple approach for calculating the BER in WDM-RZ systems, where the principal nonlinear impairment is collision-induced timing jitter. This approach produces BERs that are accurate to within one order of magnitude.

articleTitle: OSNR and jitter tolerant all-optical clock recovery at 40 Gbit/s using a quantum-dots based self-pulsating laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally analyze the jitter suppression effect of an all-optical clock recovery based on quantum-dots self-pulsating laser in the presence of optical noise and show a full operation down to an input OSNR of 22 dB/0.1 nm

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of XPM-induced birefringence in mixed-fiber transparent optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The impact of XPM-induced birefringence on 10 Gb/s NRZ intensity modulated transparent optical networks is investigated. The impairments are experimentally measured for different inline dispersion compensation maps and realistic setups with SSMF or mixed fiber.

articleTitle: Absorber length optimisation for sub-picosecond pulse generation and ultra-low jitter performance in passively mode-locked 1.3 /spl mu/m quantum-dot laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Through absorber length optimisation, sub-picosecond pulse generation and ultra-low timing jitter are demonstrated in a 20 GHz passive mode-locked quantum-dot laser diode. Pulsewidths as low as 796 fs and timing jitter performance of 390 fs (20 kHz-50 MHz) are achieved

articleTitle: Network design for large data flow
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: SURFnet6, the new national research network in the Netherlands is based on a hybrid network architecture. This network economically delivers both end-to-end lightpath services and layer3 IP services over a shared optical infrastructure.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s and 40 Gb/s WDM multi-casting using a hybrid integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: WDM multi-casting is experimentally demonstrated by performing all-optical simultaneous multi-wavelength conversion at 10 Gb/s and 40 Gb/s using a hybrid integrated Mach-Zehnder interferometer. At 40 Gb/s a Q factor degradation smaller than 0.63 was obtained for all channels

articleTitle: Access transport network for IPTV video distribution
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present the results of a case study where gigabit Ethernet interfaces are combined with SONET and/or fiber infrastructure to offer better network economics for IPTV video delivery by service providers in the access network.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional optical code processing in MPLS photonic routers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A multi-dimensional passive encoder/decoder has been characterized that can generate/process about 13000 different labels, with a label processing speed of 13.3 Glabel/s and a packet loss probability of 10/sup -9/ for a SNR of 23 dB.

articleTitle: Reducing the OBGP protection switching time in WDM mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, a fast protection switching scheme based on the parallel restoration signaling, parallel restoration scheme (PRS), is introduced into the optical border gateway protocol (OBGP) in survivable optical mesh networks. In the PRS, the message for resource reservation along the backup lightpath is forwarded to the upstream autonomous system (AS) ahead of the optical cross connects (OXC) reconfiguration when the working path fails. Compared with the traditional serial restoration scheme (SRS), the PRS can reduce the mean time of protection switching from the working path to the backup path according to theory analyses and simulation experiments. Numerical results demonstrate that the protection time is decreased by more than 50%, if the PRS is applied.

articleTitle: PMD rules for physical constraint-based routing in all optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: PMD rules are developed from transmission modeling, enabling a fast and accurate estimate of the PMD penalty with and without mitigation, which are well suited for the physical constraint-based routing computation

articleTitle: Optical network foundation for triple play services roll-out
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Telecom carriers worldwide are engaged in the IP transformation of their legacy network infrastructure for consolidation and to enable the wide deployment of new triple play high-speed services (e.g. IPTV, VOD, VoIP). One of the challenges facing carriers is that triple play enabled networks are fundamentally different from their predecessors. They need to carry a multitude of high-bandwidth services over a single network, and unlike traditional point-to-point connections, triple play networks are much more distributed, multi-point, and broader in scope. For these reasons, new IP/MPLS infrastructures to address triple play roll-outs is not enough - carriers need to make sure that they also have the right agile optical transport foundation in place to support these new dynamic high-bandwidth services. This paper explores the demands and requirements that triple play broadband services are placing on the optical metro infrastructure. It also presents the key networking attributes of the underlining optical metro/regional network (e.g. ROADM) required to deal with the unprecedented triple play broadband demands.

articleTitle: 3-port WDM filter arrays based on novel planar lightwave circuit assembly technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel configuration of ultra-compact 1310/1490/1550-nm WDM filter arrays compounded of a thin-film filter and two planar lightwave circuits. By using simple assembly techniques to optimize the arrangement, the insertion loss less than 0.7 dB is successfully achieved.

articleTitle: Error-free spectral encoding and decoding operation of InP O-CDMA encoder
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report error-free spectral encoding and decoding operation of an InP monolithic, ultra-compact optical-CDMA encoder/decoder photonic chip pair. The experimental results demonstrate the strong potential for realizing high performance O-CDMA networks with InP micro-systems.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Anomalous Dispersion in a Solid, Silica-based Fiber at λ & lt; 1300 nm
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the first all-solid (non-holey), silica-based fiber with anomalous-dispersion (+60ps/nm-km) at wavelengths (1080nm) where silica material dispersion is negative. We demonstrate its functionality as a critical enabler for an all-fiber, Yb-based, femtosecond ring laser.

articleTitle: Polarization properties of photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Photonic crystal fibers provide increased range of mode-field diameters for passive and active fibers. At present, single mode photonic crystal fibers with mode field diameters ranging from sub-micron to beyond 40 /spl mu/m have been demonstrated. For a number of applications, it is desirable to introduce polarization maintaining properties of such fibers. In this presentation, we report on the latest development within this area and explain the design and characteristics of different types of photonic crystal fibers with both polarization-maintaining and polarizing properties.

articleTitle: 40 dB gain S-band depressed-cladding EDFA with double-pass configuration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An efficient S-band depressed-cladding erbium-doped fiber amplifier with a double-pass configuration has been realized with a peak gain of 40 dB at 1512 nm. The EDFA performances have been analyzed for different signal configurations

articleTitle: Quantum key distribution for reconfigurable optical networks (invited)
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent advances in quantum key distribution (QKD) systems for optical networks are presented including a system that is compatible with dynamic reconfiguration of the quantum channel using optical switches

articleTitle: FTTH design metrics for greenfield deployments
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: As fiber-to-the home networks are becoming more widely deployed, minimizing the cost and time of that deployment has become paramount. Every design choice the engineer makes about products or installation methods has a ripple effect that extends to the financial model. Understanding these effects enables designers to create better networks and help entrepreneurs to create more profitable businesses. To this end, the authors have created both quantitative and qualitative models to assess the merits of FTTH designs. By holding baseline factors stable and altering one variable at a time, the individual impact on cost and deployment time is demonstrated. Compounded optimization is then demonstrated by altering multiple variables, simultaneously.

articleTitle: DWDM system architecture and design trade-offs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The architecture of metropolitan transport equipment is evolving based on the changing requirements needed to support a high bandwidth access infrastructure that is video rich and the availability of a new generation of optical components including wavelength switches

articleTitle: Scalability of carrier-distributed WDM-PON for Ethernet services; GbE to future 100 GbE
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally and theoretically clarify the spectrum sliced effect which is characteristic of all loopback networks. By considering this effect, the scalability of carrier-distributed WDM-PON is discussed for GbE, 10 GbE, and 100 GbE services.

articleTitle: Localization of fiber failures in WDM PON by reusing downstream light sources
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a simple and cost-effective technique to detect and localize the fiber failures in WDM passive optical networks. By reusing the downstream lasers as WDM light sources for the optical time-domain reflectometry, the proposed technique can localize the failures in both feeder and drop fibers without using the expensive tunable laser.

articleTitle: Field trials with channel bit rates of 160 Gbit/s
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present two 8/spl times/170 Gbit/s DWDM/OTDM (1.28 Tbit/s) field transmission experiment both over more than 400 km in commercially operated legacy networks of France Telecom (FT) and Deutsche Telekom (DT), respectively. Conventional EDFA based amplification schemes as well as distributed Raman amplified systems are tested. For different levels of polarization mode dispersion due to different quality of the installed fibre infrastructure adaptive PMD compensation and polarization de-multiplexing is tested.

articleTitle: Multicast design method using multiple shared-trees in OBS networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a dynamic OBS multicast design method using multiple shared-trees, which includes shared-tree creation/selection and wavelength assignment, for the purpose of simplification of routing process and efficient accommodation of multicast traffic.

articleTitle: Resources optimization of integration of separate optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Multiple networks create redundancy in fibre resources. Merging of networks becomes a necessity. Simulation was made to evaluate options of interconnection. Through interconnections, fibre links can be eliminated. Required network resources are greatly reduced.

articleTitle: All-optical ultra-fast 2/spl times/2 switch based on XPM-induced polarization rotation in highly nonlinear fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An all-optical ultra-fast 2/spl times/2 spatial switch based on polarization rotation induced by cross-phase-modulation in highly non-linear fiber is presented. Bit-error-rate measurements confirm the effectiveness of the proposed scheme and its suitability in cascaded configurations.

articleTitle: Recent advances in avalanche photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This study presents recent advances in avalanche photodiodes. Device characterization, APD simulation results, device models, and optical receiver applications for Gb/s communication systems are also discussed

articleTitle: All-optical label recognition with SOA-MZI multistage switching scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: All-optical label recognition was successfully demonstrated for two-bit label in a time domain with a combination of a multistage switching fabric and a serial-to-parallel optical converter, both of which utilized SOA-MZI switches as a 1times2 switching element

articleTitle: A simple analytical model for PMD temporal evolution
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We introduce a simple two-parameter analytical model for the time dynamics of polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and PMD-induced penalty based on the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and demonstrate that it provides good agreement between theory, simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: Demonstration and evaluation of all-optical digital-to-analog conversion using pulse pattern recognition based on optical correlation processing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate and evaluate the all-optical digital-to-analog conversion using pulse pattern recognition based on optical correlation processing. Experimental results show that four-bit digital signals with 1.65 ps interval can be successfully converted to analog signals

articleTitle: Reconfigurable all-optical packet switching based on fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report an all-optical bit-serial packet switched system which uses a fiber Bragg grating (FBG)-based reconfigurable device to recognize optical headers. The decoder is compatible with fixed SSFBG header encoders and has a reconfiguration time of < 2 s

articleTitle: Compatibility of flat-passband, 200 GHz-wide selective switch for 160 Gb/s transmission rates
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We characterize a 200 GHz channel grid, wavelength-selective 4/spl times/1 switch with wide/flat passbands and low chromatic dispersion (|CD|<10 ps/nm) for 160 Gb/s transmission rates. Our findings indicate that the penalties associated with ISI and dispersion are very high.

articleTitle: Inter-layer communication for improving restoration time in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The restoration time in high capacity optical networks has to be kept as short as possible in order to avoid a huge loss of data. This paper discusses several methods to improve restoration time in optical networks and we propose the use of error codes that will trigger immediately the appropriate layer recovery mechanism, which is the best to handle a given fault.

articleTitle: Novel techniques for optical packet generation with high-spectral efficiency and high receiver sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report generation and transmission of high-spectral efficiency and high receiver sensitivity optical packet with 25 GHz frequency spacing between 40 Gbit/s payload and 2.5 Gbit/s label by using novel enabling techniques.

articleTitle: Actively stabilized Brillouin fiber laser with high output power and low noise
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an actively stabilized Brillouin fiber ring laser with high power and low noise. Significant reduction (/spl sim/20 dB) of both relative intensity noise (RIN) and frequency noise was observed in the Brillouin Stokes radiation with linewidth of 200 Hz.

articleTitle: 160 Gb/s Raman-assisted notch-filtered XPM wavelength conversion and transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In-line wavelength conversion of 160 Gb/s data by Raman-assisted notch-filtered XPM is demonstrated for 130 km total transmission. The improvement in system performance from applying Raman gain during conversion is shown.

articleTitle: Compact 1.31&1.49/1.55 /spl mu/m WDM using fiber type lens
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By using fiber collimator with graded index fiber type lens and applying the simple fabrication process, the compact 1.31&1.49/1.55 /spl mu/m WDM have been achieved. This WDM exhibits low insertion loss, high isolation and high reliability.

articleTitle: Proposal of RoF transmission system using 850 nm VCSEL and 1.3 /spl mu/m SMF with low-frequency superposition technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel RoF transmission system with a combination of 850 nm VCSEL and 1.3 /spl mu/m SMF. Using the low-frequency superposition technique, we demonstrate the RoF transmission of OFDM-64QAM signal with significant reduction of modal noise and distortions.

articleTitle: A large mode area elliptical hollow photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on the design, fabrication and characterization of an elliptical hollow photonic crystal fiber (EH-PCF), a PCF with an elliptical hole in its solid core, for applications requiring large mode area and high birefringence

articleTitle: Efficient generation of CW supercontinuum in optical fiber pumped by ASE light
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new and efficient approach to generation of a continuous-wave supercontinuum in optical fiber pumped by an amplified spontaneous emission light. A bandwidth of 268 nm (at -15 dB level) with an average spectral density of 2.7 mW/nm is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Increased amplifier efficiency by matching the area of the doped fiber region with the fundamental fiber mode
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A significant improvement in the efficiency of high power large-mode area fiber amplifiers is demonstrated by improving the overlap of the doped region with the fundamental mode of the fiber

articleTitle: Ribbon vs. loose tube fiber cabling
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In the distribution portion of the passive optical network (PON) for fiber-to-the-premise (FTTP) architectures, the choice of fiber cabling ribbon vs. loose tube - can directly impact ease of installation and future performance. As is usually the case in these networks, specific architectural characteristics and particular applications may dictate the deployment of one type of cable over the other. However, ADC's experience in developing and manufacturing FTTP network equipment has concluded that in most cases, ribbon cable provides a considerable performance advantage over loose tube in the distribution portion of the PON network. This document will focus on fiber density and hybrid design and will discuss in detail the fiber requirements of connectorized distribution.

articleTitle: Wavelength and width-tunable optical pulses generated from four-wave mixing in a 35-cm bismuth oxide highly nonlinear optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a 10-GHz optical pulsed source based on four-wave mixing in a 35-cm bismuth-oxide based highly nonlinear optical fiber. The pulse width is continuously tunable from 22 to 46 ps over a wavelength range of 10 nm

articleTitle: Scaling of Most-Likely Traffic Patterns of Hose- and Cost-Constrained Ring and Mesh Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report analytical results and statistical comparisons for the solution to the hose- and cost-constrained inverse problem for the traffic matrix and distance-dependence of ring and mesh networks based on the method of maximum entropy.

articleTitle: 16 /spl times/ 1.25 Gbit/s WDM-PON based on ASE-injected R-SOAs in 60/spl deg/C temperature range
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A specially designed R-SOA with high gain and wider modulation bandwidth is introduced. The injection power requirement and the viable temperature range are experimentally analysed in 16 /spl times/ 1.25 Gbit/s WDM-PON based on ASE-injected R-SOAs.

articleTitle: FTTH remote fiber monitoring using optical wavelength domain reflectometry (OWDR) and wavelength coded tag (WCT)
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
