abstract: A TFF-based novel 2-port wavelength coded tag (WCT) is proposed and demonstrated. Optical wavelength domain reflectometry that relies on WCT to differentiate fiber failure from terminal equipment failure for FTTH network remote monitoring applications is also described.

articleTitle: Field trial of a 1250-km private optical network based on a single-fiber, shared-amplifier WDM system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the first field trial of an ultra-longhaul WDM transmission system with a single-fiber, shared-amplifier architecture over a fourteen-span, 1250-km optical link with mixed fiber types for remote data replication in storage area networks.

articleTitle: Optimized traffic grooming as a way to mitigate the effect of chromatic dispersion in metro/regional WDM networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose optimized traffic grooming to mitigate the effect of chromatic dispersion in WDM networks. We show an example where 34% network cost reduction is achieved in comparison to the use of dispersion compensating fibers.

articleTitle: Reducing the backreflection impact by using gain-saturated SOA in WDM single-fiber loopback access networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reduces the impact of backreflection in WDM single-fiber loopback access networks by using a gain-saturated SOA. We presented the concept and experimentally confirmed that the gain-saturated SOA significantly improves the SNR of upstream signal

articleTitle: Effect of residual dispersion and phase response ripple at 40 Gb/s using a tunable chirped fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: It is shown analytically and experimentally that the proper amount of residual dispersion can mitigate the power penalty induced by the phase response ripple of a tunable dispersion compensating fiber Bragg grating

articleTitle: Split-step quasi-spectral finite difference method for nonlinear optical pulse propagation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using finite differences with quasi-spectral properties, a new split-step method with optimum complexity for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation is presented. For accurate simulations of large WDM systems, substantial speed-up factors over the split-step Fourier method are obtained.

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion monitoring technique using birefringent fiber loop
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A chromatic dispersion monitoring technique using birefringent fiber loop is proposed. An unambiguous measurement range of 1500-ps/nm for 10-Gb/s NRZ signal is demonstrated without transmitter modification. This technique can be used to monitor multiple channels.

articleTitle: Fault-localization in WDM-PONs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a fault-localization method in wavelength division multiplexing passive optical networks. We detect the fault position using a wavelength-locked Fabry-Perot laser diode as a tunable probe light.

articleTitle: High efficiency, wide range and completely transparent wavelength conversion method using replicas generated by dual pump nearly-degenerated four-wave mixing in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer SOA
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The novel technique for completely transparent wavelength conversion using replicas by dual pump nearly-degenerated FWM in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer SOA has enabled 16-nm conversion of a 10-Gb/s signal with high efficiency of -6.0 dB.

articleTitle: Flexible 10.7 Gb/s DWDM transmission over up to 1200 km without optical in-line or post-compensation of using MLSE-EDC
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 50 GHz DWDM transmission at 10.7 Gb/s over up to 1200 km on NZ-DSF without optical in-line or post-compensation is demonstrated with duobinary signals and receiver-based MLSE-EDC, with system flexibility suitable for add/drop optical networking.

articleTitle: Novel dispersion compensating fiber with fluorine-doped cladding for simultaneous realization of high dispersion compensation efficiency and low attenuation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Fluorine-doped cladding with a /spl Delta//sup -/ of -0.2% was employed for the dispersion compensation fiber with triple-cladding structure, which successfully realized the dispersion less than -300 ps/km/nm while keeping a figure of merit higher than 350 ps/nm/dB.

articleTitle: Transfer of orbital angular momentum between acoustic and optical vortices in optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Transfer of orbital angular momentum from an electronically controlled acoustic vortex to an optical vortex in optical fiber is experimentally demonstrated. Potential applications include quantum key encryption and decoding and optical trapping

articleTitle: Optimal utility-based bandwidth allocation over integrated optical and WiMAX networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present an optimal utility-based bandwidth allocation scheme for VoD services over an experimental integrated optical and wireless broadband network. We formulate the problem using integer programming, and propose an efficient dynamic programming approach to find the optimal solution.

articleTitle: Elimination of data pattern dependence in SOA-based differential-mode wavelength converters using optically-induced birefringence
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a technique for eliminating nonlinear-pattern-dependence in SOA-based differential-mode wavelength-converters using optically-induced polarization rotation. Power penalty improvement of 2.6 dB for 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</sup>-1 PRBS data is achieved by compensating for 3.3 dB pattern dependence

articleTitle: Athermal AWGs for colourless WDM-PON with -40 ° C to +70 ° C and underwater operation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Athermal AWGs are ideal candidates for MUX/DEMUX in WDM-PON applications being passive, scalable, cyclic and low cost. This paper demonstrates an AWG with -40°C to 70°C and underwater operation in all C, L, S and E-bands.

articleTitle: Suppression of intrachannel nonlinearities using BCJR algorithm and iterative decoding
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: MAP symbol decoding supplemented with iterative decoding is used to mitigate the intrachannel nonlinearities. The MAP detector operates on the channel trellis to correct the corrupted data and to provide soft outputs processed further in an iterative decoder. A dramatic performance improvement is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Architectural and economic impact of the integration of SONET and DWDM platforms
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The emerging architecture that integrates SONET and DWDM in a single transport system is explored. The architectural implications and economic consequences of the integration are analyzed. Real-world examples are used in support of the analyses.

articleTitle: Monolithic vertical integration of metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor with subterranean photonics in silicon
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Monolithic integration of photonics and electronics has been achieved in silicon by vertically integrating metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors and waveguide-coupled microdisk resonators in a double-layer silicon-on-insulator wafer, thus paving the way towards dense three-dimensional optoelectronic integration

articleTitle: Distribution of Fiber-Generated Polarization Entangled Photon-Pairs over 100 km of Standard Fiber in OC-192 WDM Environment
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate distribution of polarization entanglement over 100 km in a WDM environment. Two-photon interference with visibility >90% is observed in coincidence detection of photon-pairs that have traveled with classical data signals, one on adjacent channel.

articleTitle: Demonstration of asynchronous ultrahigh speed optical label switching using SSFBGs label recognizer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time, we experimentally demonstrated asynchronous ultrahigh speed optical label switching using 4 SSFBGs label recognizers with the guard time of 3 ns. We also confirmed that the optical label recognizer/processor can operate for optical label after 40 km of SMF transmission without dispersion compensation

articleTitle: An efficient all-fiber interleaving filter using fiber Gires-Tournois etalons on a Michelson interferometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the use of fiber Gires-Tournois etalons on a Michelson interferometer for the implementation of an all-fiber 25/50 GHz interleaving filter with a 0.5 dB passband bandwidth of 18.5 GHz, Q-factor of 92.5 %, and channel isolation of 24 dB.

articleTitle: Dispersion tolerant alternative 10-Gb/s transmitters and implications for WDM optical networking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review some of the recently introduced 10-Gb/s transmitters and techniques that allow wide dispersion tolerances. We examine the implications of using such solutions in optical networks and enumerate potential benefits as well as limitations.

articleTitle: Broad-bandwidth Brillouin slow light in optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that Brillouin slow light with an arbitrary large bandwidth can be readily obtained in conventional optical fibers using a simple and inexpensive pump spectral broadening technique.

articleTitle: Degree-4 node using a single wavelength-selective switch
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a degree-4 node using a single 1×7 wavelength-selective switch. This is a factor of four reduction in main component count over conventional designs, but demands must be symmetric, and individual channel power control is not possible.

articleTitle: A sixteen-user time-slotted SPECTS O-CDMA network testbed
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a time-slotted SPECTS O-CDMA network testbed supporting up to 16 users at 10 Gb/s/user. Error-free performance is achieved using a NOLM time gate and a nonlinear thresholder and without FEC.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating technologies and applications in sensors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review recent advances in development of fibre grating based optical biosensor devices and applications. The emphases will be on novel grating structures UV-inscribed in D-shape, single and multi mode, and multicore fibres and their post-sensitisation by HF-etching technique. Some of these devices have been used to detect concentration of hemoglobin protein in sugar solution, showing a sensitivity as high as 20 nm/1%

articleTitle: Tunable optical CDMA encoder/decoder based on modified PN code using FBG array
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel tunable OCDMA encoder/decoder based on modified PN code FBG array. Bragg wavelengths of the FBG array are tuned by strain/temperature control and selected by a band-pass filter to realize the full-set of user codes.

articleTitle: Enhanced passive mode-locking of fiber lasers using carbon nanotubes deposited onto D-shaped fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel passive mode-locking enhanced by the interaction of carbon-nanotubes with the evanescent-field of propagating beam in a D-shaped fiber. The scheme featuring long lateral interaction guarantees strong nonlinear effect from the nanotubes.

articleTitle: Optical multicasting and full-mesh wavelength-routing over asymmetric star topology network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate the implementation of two functions in a CWDM star-shaped wavelength-routing network, namely optical multicasting and optimization for unequal node distances from the wavelength router, and improved applicability to metro area networks.

articleTitle: Maximized optical stream share of multicast videos for reducing buffer and packet processing in WDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Performances of video delivery in WDM-PON can be enhanced by maximizing optical stream share of multicast videos. With adaptive multicast channel swapping and VLAN operation, data buffer size and packet processing are meaningfully reduced.

articleTitle: A 17-Gb/s low-power optical receiver using a Ge-on-SOI photodiode with a 0.13- μm CMOS IC
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the fastest (17Gb/s) and lowest-voltage (1.8V) all-silicon CMOS optical receiver to date, based on a germanium-on-SOI photodiode. The 12.5-Gb/s sensitivity at 850nm is -12.7dBm (BER=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>), with a power consumption as low as 50mW.

articleTitle: Ultra high gain fiber optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A record optical fiber gain of 70 dB is achieved using a continuous wave pumped fiber optical parametric amplifier. Limitations due to saturation effects in this unidirectional amplifier are also discussed

articleTitle: Optical parallel processing approach to all-order PMD compensation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe our research on PMD compensation and sensing using a parallel optical frequency domain approach and review our recent experiments on compensation of 600 fs pulses broadened to >2 ps via all-order PMD

articleTitle: First experimental demonstration of combined multicast and unicast video streaming over an optical-label switching network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper experimentally demonstrates, for the first time to our knowledge, the combined multicast and unicast video streaming applications over an optical-label switching network, with edge routers connecting the end-to-end multicast server and clients.

articleTitle: Low-complexity hybrid MLSE equalizers for 10 Gb/s Ethernet multi-mode fiber links
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a new class of electronic equalizers for 10 Gb/s multi-mode fiber links that combine the advantages of Viterbi equalizers and decision feedback equalizers (DFE) yielding a low complexity, readily implemented architecture with performance /spl sim/0.5-0.75 dBo better than an infinite-length DFE.

articleTitle: Silicon-based monolithic 4/spl times/4 wavelength-selective cross connect with on-chip micromirrors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A monolithic 4/spl times/4 wavelength-selective cross-connect (chip area = 3.2/spl times/4.6 cm ) is realized by integrating four 4/spl times/1 MEMS wavelength-selective switches and four 1/spl times/4 passive splitters, together with a 4/spl times/4 waveguide shuffle network on a silicon-on-insulator. Wavelength-selective routing has been successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Multi-path, multi-wavelength packet routing at 40 Gb/s over an SOA based optical switch fabric with nanosecond reconfiguration time
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The first multi-path physical layer assessment of a multiple host routing system employing an optical switch fabric is reported. 40 Gb/s data is routed from three inputs with wavelength and path dependant crosstalk contributing 0.3-0.6 dB penalty.

articleTitle: On performance of coherent phase-shift-keying modulation in 40 Gb/s long-haul optical fiber transmission systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare the performance of coherent binary-phase-shift-keying and incoherent differential-binary-phase-shift-keying formats in linear and nonlinear 40-Gb/s systems. We show that intra-channel nonlinear interactions severely degrade the coherent binary-phase-shift-keying performance in highly nonlinear systems

articleTitle: RF video overlay in an Ethernet passive optical network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper studies the effects of non-linear Raman cross-talk in an RF video overlay in an Ethernet based passive optical network. We show that the Raman cross-talk between the 1490 nm and the 1550 nm wavelengths and the presence of idle frames seriously limits analog video transmission at some specific frequencies. Digital video transmission based on quadrature amplitude modulation is possible, however.

articleTitle: Incoherent microwave photonic filters with complex coefficients using stimulated Brillouin scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate for the first time to our knowledge an incoherent microwave photonic filter with complex coefficients. The technique is based on a controllable optically-induced RF phase shift by means of stimulated Brillouin scattering

articleTitle: Packet-by-packet all-optical burst-mode 3R regeneration in an optical-label switching router
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper demonstrates 10 Gb/s packet-by-packet burst-mode optical 3R regeneration in an optical-label switching router, achieving bit-error-rates below 1/spl times/10/sup -9/ with the guard time ranging from 50 to 1000 ns despite clock-phase discontinuity between packets.

articleTitle: Optical networking testbeds in China
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: National R&D activities on optical networking testbeds in China, including CAINONET, 3Tnet and OBS testbed, are described for investigating key technologies of next generation optical networking.

articleTitle: Phase stabilisation of coherent WDM modulator array
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reports for the first time a simple stabilisation circuitry technique to monitor and control the relative phase between adjacent channels in a coherent WDM transmitter, achieving optimum performance.

articleTitle: Pulse propagation effects at high bit rates
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The constant drive to increase bit rate per channel faces significant challenges due to linear and nonlinear propagation effects. Shorter pulses increase the sensitivity to dispersion effects including higher order, polarization mode dispersion and fiber nonlinearity.

articleTitle: The European network of excellence e-Photon/ONe on optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: e-Photon/ONe is a network of excellence (NoE) on optical networks funded by the EU. NoEs aim at fostering integration of the activities of involved researchers and institutions, exploiting complementarity to achieve critical mass. "Virtual departments" in e-Photon/ONe coordinate research activities on specific thematic areas.

articleTitle: A comparison of optical packet switching node architectures based on component cost
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper we discuss the node architecture costs of two all-optical packet switching nodes, a node with electronic header processing and the IP over WDM approach. We compare the costs for increasing network traffic.

articleTitle: All-optical M-ary ASK signal demultiplexer based on photonic analog-to-digital conversion with bitwise signal allocation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate the all-optical M-ary ASK signal demultiplexer based on photonic analog-to-digital conversion with bitwise signal allocation. Experimental result shows that the quaternary ASK signal can be successfully demultiplexed into two 25 Gb/s OOK signals

articleTitle: Resilience in all-optical label swapping networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: All-optical label swapping is a promising packet-switching technology but has as main disadvantage that nodes can be very component-consuming. This paper deals with dimensioning the all-optical nodes when the all-optical network is made resilient

articleTitle: Analytical investigation of optimization, performance bound, and chromatic dispersion tolerance of 4-amplitude-shifted-keying format
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By using Karhunen-Loeve expansion and saddlepoint approximation methods, we show the optimal optical and electrical receiver bandwidth, optimal multilevel spacing, bit-error-probability bound, and the superior tolerance to the chromatic dispersion of 4-amplitude-shifted-keying format.

articleTitle: RF-photonic generation of high-power ultrawideband arbitrary waveforms using predistortion
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By employing a predistortion technique tailored to a fiber dispersion based RF-photonic arbitrary waveform generator, we experimentally obtained desired ultrawideband RF waveforms with voltage amplitudes of more than 13 V in the presence of substantial gain and phase distortion

articleTitle: A 2-m-long reshaping regenerator based on a highly nonlinear bismuth oxide fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the use of a 2-m-long highly nonlinear bismuth oxide fiber in a simple 2R regeneration scheme. An improvement in receiver sensitivity of ~5 dB at 10-Gbit/s and ~2 dB at 40-Gbit/s is demonstrated

articleTitle: Spectral dependence of polarization hole-burning
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a simple experimental approach to measure and quantify the polarization hole-burning in an optical amplifier. The spectral properties of polarization hole-burning are similar to those of spectral hole-burning

articleTitle: Optical code generation using longitudinal mode modulation of 40 Gbps mode-locked laser diode
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical code generation and discrimination at 40 Gbps were experimentally demonstrated using longitudinal mode modulation of MLLD in time-spread/wavelength-hopping optical code. The crosstalk of cross correlation after fiber transmission for 30 km was less than 10 dB.

articleTitle: An experimental analysis of performance fluctuations in high-capacity repeaterless WDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present an investigation of performance fluctuations in high-capacity repeaterless WDM systems. In a 32/spl times/12.3 Gb/s 410 km transmission experiment, nonlinear channel cross-talk causes > 1.5 dB Q-factor fluctuation. System design must include sufficient margin for these fluctuations.

articleTitle: All-optical signal processing based on self-induced effects in a vertical cavity semiconductor switch
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate all-optical seed-pulse extractor for DPSK and OOK packet synchronization and all-optical header extractor at 10 Gbit/s exploiting a novel approach based on self-induced effect in passive, low-power, polarization-independent, compact vertical cavity semiconductor switch.

articleTitle: Automatic installation in QKD system using photon-counting optical power meter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A burst-length-setting and phase-optimization technique were proposed for use in QKD, and we demonstrated their repeatability. QKD could automatically be installed on a strange optical line with these techniques.

articleTitle: Distributed Raman amplification on fiber with large connector losses
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simplified formula for the gain and noise figure of distributed Raman amplification on fibers with large connector losses is derived. It is shown that OTDR measurements are required to estimate the available Raman gain

articleTitle: Numerical and experimental study of an alternate multiwavelength mode-locked fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the experimental generation of alternate multiwavelength pulse trains in a mode-locked fiber ring laser containing an unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometer at an aggregate repetition rate of 18.8 GHz. These results are compared with simulations.

articleTitle: Gain reshaping caused by spectral hole burning in long EDFA-based transmission links
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show that the effect of SHB on power evolution in long-haul EDFA-based links is largest in the first few spans, saturating with distance, and that its strength on end-to-end gain depends on number of amplifiers and not EDFA gain.

articleTitle: Novel concept for all-optical clock recovery from NRZ format PRBS data streams
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Synchronization of a self-pulsating phaseCOMB-laser to NRZ data signals is demonstrated for the first time. The clock signal extracted from 40 Gb/s PRBS stream shows a good timing stability in a wide input power range.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency laser monolithically integrating InGaAsP gain elements with amorphous silicon AWG
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a photonic integrated circuit using a novel monolithic integration platform combining InGaAsP gain elements and index matched amorphous silicon waveguide devices. The AWG based multi-frequency laser emits eight 100-GHz-spaced wavelengths near 1550 nm.

articleTitle: Linearity and ultra-linearization of ring resonator modulators for sub-octave bandpass analog optical links
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The linearity of a ring resonator based modulator is experimentally studied. From the experimental transfer function, the intermodulation-free dynamic range is predicted to be 123 dBHz/sup 4/5/. A scheme to obtain ultra-high linearity is proposed.

articleTitle: Wide-band single-mode photonic band-gap fiber with extended triangular lattice and capillary core
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a single-mode photonic band-gap fiber with an extended triangular lattice cladding and a capillary core. We numerically optimize the design of the core and show that the fiber has a very wide transmission window, such as from 1200 nm to 2300 nm

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband near-infrared emission from Bi-doped lithium alumino silicate glasses for optical amplification
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Near infrared ultra-broadband emission with the broadest bandwidth as much as 450 nm to our knowledge, has been observed from Bi-doped lithium alumino silicate glasses

articleTitle: Stabilizing a 10 GHz 0.8 ps asynchronously mode-locked Er-fiber soliton laser by deviation-frequency locking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Without using high speed RF feedback electronics, long-term stabilization of a 10 GHz 0.8 ps mode-locked Er-fiber soliton laser with asynchronous phase modulation is demonstrated by controlling the cavity length to lock the deviation frequency at 25 kHz

articleTitle: Large area higher-order-mode fibers for bend-resistant, broadband transmission and pulse compression
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a higher-order-mode fiber-based platform, to achieve low-loss, bend-resistant, mode-coupling-free light transmission over meter-length fibers, in a record A<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> of 2100 mum<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Its nonlinearity tolerance is demonstrated by compressing fiber-laser pulses to 64 fs, yielding 52-kW peak powers

articleTitle: Observation of ignition induced by a high power light input at a butt-joint splice with refractive index matching material
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We evaluate the robustness of a butt-joint splice with refractive index matching material when a high power light is input and observe the ignition thus induced

articleTitle: External cavity wavelength tunable laser utilizing on-chip VOA
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated an external cavity wavelength tunable laser using a novel gain chip with monolithically integrated VOA function. Over 15-dBm output power and an output power tuning range of 55 dB were obtained over the whole C-band.

articleTitle: A novel strain- and temperature-sensing mechanism based on dynamic grating in polarization-maintaining erbium-doped fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The first experimental observation of dynamic grating in polarization-maintaining erbium-doped fiber (PM-EDF) is reported and a novel fiber-optic strain- and temperature-sensing mechanism based on the dynamic grating in PM-EDF is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-based erbium doped fiber for short pulse amplification
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate short pulse amplification, and compare the nonlinear tolerance of a Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based erbium doped fiber (EDF) with a conventional silica-based EDF. The Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-based EDF shows highly nonlinear tolerance and superior short pulse amplification performances

articleTitle: Low-threshold CW 1.55-/spl mu/m GaAs-based lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the first low-threshold continuous-wave (CW) 1.55-/spl mu/m GaAs-based lasers. Using a single GaInNAsSb quantum well as the active region, edge-emitting lasers yielded CW thresholds as low as 579 A/cm/sup 2/ (550 A/cm/sup 2/ pulsed) and output powers > 100 mW.

articleTitle: 2-to-many lossless optical multicast using an optical crosspoint switch matrix
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 2-to-many optical multicast without splitting loss is demonstrated using optical crosspoint switch matrix. Power penalty of < 4.5 dB is found in switched signals. The measured results confirm the excellent switching and multicasting characteristics of this device.

articleTitle: Square core jacketed air-clad fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the fabrication of a square core jacketed air-clad fiber with a top-hat near-field intensity profile. Using this fiber we have successfully produced square shaped ablation marks in ITO without complex beam shaping optics.

articleTitle: Components for quantum cryptography
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a new protocol for practical quantum cryptography, tailored for a high key generation rate using weak coherent pulses. We discuss the required features of the optical key components of the system

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of simultaneous all-optical frequency conversion for full-duplex WDM RoF systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Simultaneous all-optical frequency up- and down-conversions of an optical IF signal and an optical RF signal to the upper and lower frequency band, respectively, using a single SOA-MZI without serious crosstalk were experimentally demonstrated and a concept of cost-effective full-duplex WDM radio-over-fiber (RoF) link utilizing a simultaneous up/downconversion is proposed. The experimental results show a potential of the proposed scheme for use in a cost-effective full-duplex WDM RoF link without performance degradation.

articleTitle: Design of MPLS/GMPLS multilayer network considering protection and restoration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents a study on the design of an MPLS/GMPLS multilayer network. This paper evaluates the impact of the optical path creation policy according to the electrical path demand considering optical path protection and restoration.

articleTitle: Evidence of noise compression by cross gain compression in SOAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Effective compression of the noise distributions in optical NRZ signals by exploiting cross-gain-compression in SOAs is reported. First transmission results show that this simple technique can be used for all-optical 2R regeneration without wavelength conversion.

articleTitle: Flexible FTTX Deployment using Segmented Ribbon and Bend Insensitive Fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Fiber to the premises deployments are growing significantly and the methodology for deployment is maturing around common denominations of ribbon of 4, 8, and 12 fibers. A new type of ribbon allowing breakouts in these denominations has been developed. The design of the new ribbon allows removal of subunit ribbons with out the risk of damage to the individual fibers. The host or subunit ribbons are then mass fusion spliced to a ribbon assembly with preconnectorized fibers in an enclosure. Drop cables are then connected and run to the premises. The demands of the route, span, and space inside each enclosure have driven the development of a new design of bend insensitive fiber for use in these cables. The combination of segmented ribbon in the distribution and feeder cables and bend insensitive fiber in the drop cable make for a more flexible and robust deployment.

articleTitle: Clock extraction from 160-Gbit/s signal using optoelectronic phase-locked loop based on optical phase modulation and spectral filtering
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel phase-locked loop (PLL) for clock extraction using an optoelectronic phase comparator based on phase modulation and spectral filtering. With such PLL, a low-noise 10-GHz clock is extracted from a 160-Gbit/s signal.

articleTitle: Broadband photonic crystal passive filters for integrated InP photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Two broadband, InP photonic crystal optical filters with reduced back-reflections are demonstrated: one 10/spl mu/m-long low-pass with 20 dB stop-band extinction; one 30 /spl mu/m-long, 40-nm bandwidth notch with 20 dB extinction. Both could find applications as band-rejection filters in monolithic InP photonic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: Fabrication of micro-channels in optical fibers using femtosecond laser pulses and selective chemical etching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The fabrication of micro-channels in single-mode optical fibers is demonstrated using focused femtosecond laser processing and chemical etching. Straight line micro-channels are achieved based on a simple technique which overcomes limitations imposed by the fiber curved surface

articleTitle: Dynamics of optically excited semiconductor optical amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time, an investigation of the recovery dynamics of semiconductor optical amplifiers explains why the ultrafast component of the gain recovery is largely absent in the phase response. This has important implications for signal processing.

articleTitle: The MV aerial power grid at VHF/UHF rivals fiber in capacity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper shows that the aerial medium voltage (MV) power grid rivals Fiber in Capacity, at UHF/VHF bands, offering measured spectral densities up to 15-20 Bps/Hz in a repeatered system, with Shannon capacities reaching OC12/OC48 rates. Its ubiquitous deployment, channelization, and the general availability of unused VHF/UHF broadcast channels, implies excellent suitability as a metro/access solution.

articleTitle: Experiences from the Acreo national Broadband Testbed
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We describe the Acreo National Broadband Testbed in Sweden. The testbed is a multi-technology end-to-end access network with more than 200 users testing real services. Technical design, experiences and visions from the testbed are presented.

articleTitle: A novel fabrication method of versatile holey fibers with low bending loss and their optical characteristics
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel fabrication method of holey fibers with different size, pitch, and shape of air holes. By expanding a Ge-doped preform with air holes at high temperature, the size and shape of air holes can be readily modified

articleTitle: Epitaxy-free 1.53, μm quantum dot laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report lasing operation of solution-processed semiconductor quantum dot films at 1.53 μm. A solid quantum dot film was used inside a hollow-core optical fibre to form a whispering gallery mode resonator.

articleTitle: Artificial defects as ingredients for synthesizing holey fibers with large mode area and flat chromatic dispersion: an emerging technology for high speed transmission platforms
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We numerically demonstrate the operation of a novel class of holey fibers with artificial defects for engineering the large mode area and flat chromatic dispersion for applications in high speed optical transmission systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic optical signal processing via a recirculating loop
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A highly reconfigurable optical signal processing circuit is introduced and implemented experimentally. The circuit utilizes a recirculating loop to implement a lattice filter of adjustable order. The response can be tuned to approximate a desired transfer matrix

articleTitle: The comparison and evaluation of textile innerduct vs. rigid innerduct installations and applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Textile innerducts, a new construction solution for the outside plant market and manufactured from monofilament yarns, promised easier cable installation compared to standard high density polyethylene (HDPE) conduits. Performance was measured by conducting controlled field testing of several configurations of textile innerducts in a variety of duct applications over the same test length. Results revealed that textile innerducts could reduce cable pulling tension by up to 60 percent over equivalent rigid innerduct products.

articleTitle: Photonic crystals for communications: stopping light and miniaturized non-reciprocal devices
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We highlight some of the new possibilities of photonic crystal for optical communication applications, including stopping, storage, and time-reversal of light, as well as miniaturized non-reciprocal devices.

articleTitle: Low beat-noise, highly polarized tunable fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A low beat-noise polarized tunable fiber ring laser is reported. The laser utilized a FP-LD to achieve 34-nm tunable range in 1.12-nm steps and 99% degree of polarization. The beat-noise was reduced dramatically by 50 dB with the FP-LD.

articleTitle: SOI technology for microring tunable filters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent results related on optical building blocks structures for nanophotonics tunable structures based on silicon on insulator material are presented. Dimensional control of such extreme high index contrast structures for applications in complex devices will be discussed.

articleTitle: Phase correcting element for intra-cavity laser beam control
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel semiconductor laser cavity concept comprising an integrated phase correcting element is proposed and demonstrated. Characterization of the design for divergence angle reduction and near-field broadening revealed an improvement of 30.8% and 10.8%, respectively.

articleTitle: High output power (2.45 watts) mid-IR fiber amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report the first demonstration of high power mid-IR (2.7 /spl mu/m) fiber amplifiers. 2.45 W of amplified output power was obtained for an input signal of 70 mW, corresponding to a net gain of 15.4 dB.

articleTitle: Polarization-independent tunable dispersion compensator comprised of a silica arrayed waveguide grating and a polymer slab
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a planar lightwave circuit tunable optical dispersion compensator that combines silica and polymer waveguides to achieve a low power consumption and low polarization dependence. We demonstrate dispersion compensation of a 10-Gb/s pluggable transceiver.

articleTitle: Technique for highly sensitive measurement of Raman gain coefficient of optical fiber using pump/signal sum-frequency lock-in-detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple technique for measuring Raman gain in short optical fibers is demonstrated. This technique applies square-wave modulation to both pump and signal and performs lock-in-detection at sum-modulation-frequency, and measures on-off gain as small as 0.0015 dB

articleTitle: The foils of Ethernet service delivery: a service provider perspective
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Successful Ethernet service providers cannot be defined solely by the backbone equipment utilized nor by the number of customers or buildings they offer service to. Success is based upon the service level agreement they offer and the meeting of that agreement terms and conditions for all customers' services. Providing a multiple of service options may not give reproducible results for all customers. Simpler services and fewer options for quality of service and class of service provide consistency across all customers and better results. The testing piece goes hand in hand with the offering of services. Simple configuration and single test sets give reproducible results that can be shared with customers and duplicated by them during their verification testing. Being able to quickly turn up customer Ethernet circuits and accurately debug and find the causes of failure or poor performance and correcting those failures or issues is another key to success. If results cannot be duplicated and issues arise the things noted in this paper should be checked and confirmed as the first steps in trouble shooting any conditions or operations.

articleTitle: 10 Gbit/s all-optical NRZ-to-RZ data format in a dark-optical-comb injected semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: All-optical 10 Gbit/s NRZ-to-RZ data-format conversion in a backward dark-optical-comb injected semiconductor optical amplifier with BER of 10/sup -13/ at receiving power of -19 dBm and a positive power penalty of 3.7 dB is primarily demonstrated.

articleTitle: An automatic gain-controlled Raman/gain-clamped SOA for metro WDM networks with changes in span loss
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An automatic gain-controlled Raman fiber amplifier/gain-clamped SOA using a feed-forward pump-control scheme is proposed. The output signal power is automatically controlled within 0.15 dB when the span loss changes from 16 dB to 26 dB

articleTitle: Field measurements of PMD using four measurement techniques
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In the last 10 years, Telcordia has conducted numerous first-order PMD (polarization mode dispersion) measurements of installed optical fibers at various locations throughout North America. The measurements were made by using test instruments based on interferometric method. This work has been reported in detail in the past NFOEC symposia. The results have been analyzed with respect to various cable designs, type of outside plant, year of manufacture, and cable manufacturers. Recently, Telcordia has had the opportunity to make additional PMD measurements on previously characterized optical fibers. The new Telcordia measurements were made by using test instruments based on four measurement techniques. The recent PMD measurements include equipment that uses the following PMD measurement techniques: wavelength scanning (fixed analyzer) with cycle counting, Jones matrix eigenanalysis, wavelength scanning (fixed analyzer) with Fourier transform, and interferometry. According to TIA (Telecommunications Industry Association) inter-laboratory round-robin PMD tests, the four methods above yield systematic and random disagreement between measurements of within /spl plusmn/ 10 % to /spl plusmn/ 20 %. This variability is stated as state-of-the-art by TIA/EIA in their FOTPs (fiber optic test procedures) describing PMD measurement methods. The new Telcordia PMD measurements are expected to provide significant additional insight as to the relationship between the four PMD test methods listed above and help contribute to the general understanding of the major approaches to modern PMD measurement techniques.

articleTitle: Effect of PDL on OSNR monitoring technique using polarization-nulling method
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyzed the probability of errors in the measured optical signal-to-noise ratios by using the polarization-nulling technique, when the amplified spontaneous emission noise is partially polarized due to the polarization-dependent loss in the transmission link

articleTitle: Interoperability and optical network performance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Interoperability is a key enabler to provision emerging end-to-end bandwidth services and next generation optical network deployment. Optical network interoperability has been demonstrated recently at various industry sponsored events (OIF Global interoperability demonstrations at Supercomm 2004 and 2005) showing the maturity of the technology and industry status. Interoperable optical networks will enable service providers to enhance provisioning and new service creation and, thus, streamline OPEX and CAPEX and optimize their existing network to support additional revenue streams.

articleTitle: Monitoring requirements for optical transparent networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The contribution addresses optical performance monitoring from a network management perspective. The applicability of optical power monitoring, spectral analysis and Q-factor measurements for fault- configuration- and performance management of optical transport entities will be discussed.

articleTitle: Widely tunable multi-channel grating cavity laser based on a light-deflector
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Widely tunable multi-channel grating cavity laser is proposed and demonstrated. It is realized by monolithically integrating all elements in an InP. Wavelength tuning of 50 nm has been successfully achieved for the 6-channel device.

articleTitle: Brillouin suppression through longitudinal structural variation in high nonlinearity silica holey fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We consider longitudinal variation in the fiber structure as a method of increasing the Brillouin linewidth and threshold within high nonlinearity silica holey fibers. Strategies to control the associated variation in nonlinearity and dispersion along the fiber length are described

articleTitle: Cross phase modulation-based, tunable wavelength conversion of 10-Gbit/s NRZ signal using 1-m bismuth oxide-based nonlinear optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the use of 1-m length of Bi/sub 2/O/sub 3/-based nonlinear fiber for implementing a 10-Gbit/s NRZ signal wavelength converter based on XPM-induced polarization rotation. No SBS suppression scheme was employed owing to a high SBS threshold of the fiber.

articleTitle: FWM wavelength conversion with pump suppression
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel scheme that significantly improves the performance of FWM wavelength conversion is proposed and demonstrated. The scheme offers substantial pump suppression and OSNR improvement and intended for ultra-fast wavelength routing and packet switching applications.

articleTitle: Cost-effective fiber-to-the-home system using remote repeater
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a FTTH system using a remote repeater that reduces customer's transmitter costs, and extends feeder reach to 60 km and split ratio to 1:256. The system employs standard PON transceivers and demonstrates good performance.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of ultra-compact Er-doped waveguide amplifier based on bismuthate glass
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have designed and evaluated two types of spiral lightwave circuits for 1-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-size high performance waveguide amplifier. Circle-spiral layout is found to show higher performance compared to square-spiral layout because of low bending loss

articleTitle: /spl pi/-phase shifted fiber Bragg grating-based optical DPSK demodulator with optically tunable phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel optical DPSK demodulator with optically tunable phase shifter based on /spl pi/-phase shifted fiber Bragg grating is proposed and demonstrated. The 10 Gb/s DPSK signal is successfully demodulated by the proposed DPSK demodulator.

articleTitle: A new QoS differentiation scheme in optical burst switching with on-the-fly path setup mechanism
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In order to meet the requirement of data grid or CD/DVD delivery which require the characteristic QoS e.g. multiple bursts transmission, we propose a new QoS differentiation scheme based on OBS/OCS integrated network architecture with on-the-fly path setup mechanism.

articleTitle: A star-ring-bus architecture for WDM fiber-wireless system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A self-healing star-ring-bus architecture for high-capacity WDM fiber-wireless system is proposed and verified experimentally. This architecture can provide reliable, flexible, and robust characteristics for large radio terminals.

articleTitle: Characterization of high-speed optical pulses based on spectral shearing interferometry in intensity modulator with bias sweeper
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 10-GHz, pico-second optical pulse trains are experimentally characterized with high sensitivity and reliability. The principle is based on phase modulation in a Mach-Zehnder modulator and spectral fringe synthesis with a bias sweeper.

articleTitle: Network architecture modeling and design
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The network architecture modeling methodology presented here introduces a quantitative measurement of service capital costs for a given architecture. This methodology allows a carrier to compare different network architectures and to clearly identify the dominate cost portions for a service.

articleTitle: Probability density functions of rotations in loop-synchronous polarization scrambling for recirculating loop experiments
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The performance in a recirculating loop with a loop-synchronous polarization scrambler is independent of the choice of probability density function (pdf) for the rotations in the polarization scrambler, unless the pdf is strongly biased

articleTitle: Suppression of stimulated Raman scattering in a high-peak-power pulsed 1060 nm fiber MOPA source with purely single-mode output using W-type fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Suppression of stimulated-Raman-Scattering in a 100 ps, 32 MHz pulsed fiber source is demonstrated. 12.5 kW of peak power was achieved in a small core single-mode ytterbium-doped fiber amplifier where the stimulated-Raman-scattering was efficiently filtered out by a W-type waveguide structure.

articleTitle: Radiation mode analysis of tilted fiber gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Based on coupled-mode theory and new sets of HE and EH radiation modes, the scattering analysis of tilted fiber gratings is developed. The result agrees with the volume current method except at small scatter angles.

articleTitle: Low loss arrayed waveguide grating with mode converters designed by wavefront matching method
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel mode converter designed with the wavefront matching method for suppressing the mode transition loss in an arrayed waveguide grating multiplexer. We fabricated and examined the multiplexer, and confirmed the loss reduction principle

articleTitle: On protecting dynamic multicast sessions in survivable mesh WDM networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel protection scheme called multicast protection through spanning paths (MPSP) for efficient multicast protection. Simulation results demonstrate the good performance of the proposed protection scheme in reducing the spare capacity for protection.

articleTitle: Limitations of scaling switching capacity by interconnecting multiple switches
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Carriers are often faced with the need to scale the switching capacity of a central office site by installing multiple switches at that site. In this paper, we first provide a strong argument that multiple colocated switches should always be interconnected together because of the uncertainty in future traffic requests. However, this results in an inefficient use of a portion of the switching capacity as a number of ports are used to interconnect the switches together (the so-called "interconnect penalty"). We develop and apply a quantitative model that analyzes the interconnection capacity required to achieve certain performance criteria as a function of traffic uncertainty. We also derive bounds on the interconnection capacity required between multiple switches for different interconnection approaches and traffic patterns. The practical implication of this work is the realization of the need to eventually deploy an additional layer of higher-capacity switches of higher switching granularity in the context of optical networks to handle high bandwidth services and relieve the capacity needs of lower granularity switches.

articleTitle: Queue size control for the LSTP-enabled GEPON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Theoretical analysis has been conducted on the queue management in the LSTP-enabled GEPON. Results reveal the impacts of traffic load, buffer size, and traffic prediction to the queue size control. Simulations also show the performance improvement over other typical proposals.

articleTitle: Silicon based lasers and amplifiers via stimulated Raman scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Light amplification and lasing are realized in silicon waveguides via stimulated Raman scattering. With a reverse biased p-i-n structure embedded in the waveguide, we achieve continuous-wave net gain and lasing in a single silicon chip.

articleTitle: Polarization-independent two-pump fiber optical amplifier with polarization diversity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a polarization independent two-pump fiber OPA based on polarization diversity. We achieve less than 0.4-dB PDG for 15.5-dB gain when the input signal polarization is swept over the Poincare sphere.

articleTitle: Novel single mode laser fabrication using focus ion beam (FIB) etching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A single mode coupled cavity laser is demonstrated using a focus ion beam (FIB) etching process. A high power vertically emitting DFB laser is also demonstrated using an angle-etch FIB process.

articleTitle: Symmetry study for optical signals with orthogonal polarizations
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally investigate the symmetry for optical signals with orthogonal polarizations. The degree-of-polarization symmetry remains intact for the orthogonal polarizations under first/higher-order PMD, whereas the symmetry of eye-closure penalty is broken under higher-order PMD.

articleTitle: 100 GHz spaced 10 Gbit/s WDM over 10 /spl deg/C to 70 /spl deg/C using an uncooled DBR laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 100 GHz spaced 10 Gbit/s (NRZ, PRBS 2/sup 31/-1) WDM transmission is demonstrated with an uncooled DBR laser. The wavelength of the laser was stabilised within 2 GHz from 10 /spl deg/C to 70 /spl deg/C using a predicting algorithm.

articleTitle: Building light-forest to support group multicast in mesh-based optical grid networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the problem of group multicasting in optical mesh networks using light-forests. Distributed concurrent light-trees are supported by a light-forest session. Our proposed linear light-trees for drop-and-continue node architecture show efficient light-forest construction.

articleTitle: Modulation characteristics of RSOA in hybrid WDM/SCM-PON optical link
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel hybrid wavelength division multiplexed/sub carrier multiplexed passive optical network is presented by using a reflective semiconductor optical amplifier (RSOA) as a modulator. Characteristics of RSOA and SFDR as an external modulator were analyzed.

articleTitle: A /sup 13/C/sub 2/H/sub 2/ frequency-stabilized, polarization-maintained 1.54 /spl mu/m erbium fiber ring laser with a new feedback system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The frequency of a 1.54-mum erbium fiber laser was stabilized to a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> absorption line by employing a new feedback system with a LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> frequency modulator and a double-balanced-mixer. The stability reached as high as 2.2 times 10 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup> for tau=100 s

articleTitle: Small-radius 90/spl deg/-bent single mode fiber for optical interconnection
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A small-radius 90/spl deg/-bent optical fiber with approximate bending radius of 1 mm and less than 0.1 dB bending losses have been demonstrated. The fiber is suitable for optical surface mount technologies in optical interconnection systems.

articleTitle: Transmission of 40 Gbps signals through metropolitan networks engineered for 10 Gbps signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A critical emerging technology for advanced DWDM systems is 40 Gbps transmission support. The use of 40 Gbps channels increases the DWDM capacity by the factor of four, supports interconnection of next generation IP routers at OC-768 and saves OpEx and CapEx due to having to deploy and maintain fewer channels to provide the same capacity, needing fewer spare transponder modules. A key design driver for 40 Gbps technology is that it should seamlessly integrate with existing 10 Gbps systems without requiring changes to the common equipment, including ROADM technology. Parameters that must be analyzed to a greater degree at the 40 Gbps transmission rate include chromatic dispersion, PMD, and filtering effects. This analysis is based on the experiment on deployment of 43 Gb/s PSBT signals over an existing 10 Gb/s DWDM system with cascaded ROADMs that we reported on last year (M. Boduch et al., 2005).

articleTitle: Broadband variable chromatic dispersion in photonic-band electro-optic waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Broadband variable chromatic dispersion in C-band frequency range is demonstrated using novel nanostructured electro-optic waveguide consisting of low-loss Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> rectangular core and Si/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> two-dimensional photonic-crystal layer controlled by voltage bias

articleTitle: Temperature independent transmission for 10 Gbps 300 m - MMF using low driving-current quantum dot laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated 10 Gbps of transmission in 300 m of multimode fiber using a temperature independent quantum dot laser with a directly modulated constant driving current. Error-free transmission and clear eye opening was maintained up to 80/spl deg/C with an optical receiver using an electric dispersion compensator.

articleTitle: Dynamic polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and PMD compensator model and their application to the study of PMD compensator speed requirement
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a dynamic polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and PMD compensator (PMDC) model that can be used to study PMDC speed effects on a PMDC performance and the speed requirement for a PMDC.

articleTitle: Uncooled, Optical Injection-Locked 1.55 μm VCSELs for Upstream Transmitters in WDM-PONs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present the first demonstration of injection-locked 1.55 μm VCSELs for operation as low-cost, stable, uncooled, and directly modulated upstream transmitters in a WDM-PON where the injection-locking light is furnished by modulated downstream signals.

articleTitle: Integrated holographic filters for flat-passband optical multiplexers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The first fully-integrated (26×4×1 mm, silica-on-silicon), single-mode, CWDM multiplexer matching performance of bulk-optical alternatives is described as are the enabling, lithographically-scribed, integrated holographic filters, which uniquely provide flat passbands without loss penalty.

articleTitle: Detection and mitigation of soft failure due to polarization-mode dispersion in optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A combination of polarization-mode dispersion (PMD) monitoring and network-layer switching managed by the control plane can reduce the outage probability due to PMD to an acceptable level for a link in an optical network, without physical-layer mitigation.

articleTitle: Monolithic spatially-filtered 10 Gbps all-optical wavelength converter with enhanced push-pull operation using dual inverted and non-inverted inputs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reports a novel all-optical 10 Gbps tunable wavelength converter that spatially filters input and converted wavelengths as well as enhanced performance due to push-pull operation at the input.

articleTitle: Simultaneous polarization mode dispersion and chromatic dispersion monitoring method in 40 Gbit/s system by polarization modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple method to monitor CD and PMD simultaneously is proposed and implemented by using two polarization-modulation pilot tones with different frequencies. It has been theoretically derived and experimentally verified that RF output power increases with GVD and DGD in sin/sup 2/ relation, and power ratio of the two pilot tones increases with GVD and decreases with DGD, thus CD and PMD can be distinguished and monitored simultaneously.

articleTitle: Utilizing path diversity in optical packet switched interconnection networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The concept of path adjustments is introduced as a mean of increasing the utilization of optical packet switched networks. Simulation results show substantial performance improvement under uniform and non-uniform traffic, and an experimental demonstration proves feasibility.

articleTitle: Monolithically integrated high speed DFB BH laser arrays for 10 Gbased LX4 application
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel DFB laser array is demonstrated for application to the 10 Gbit Ethernet LX4 scheme. The array delivers multiple mW output power and high-speed operation (3.125 Gb/s) at 85/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Propagation of 10-Gb/s RZ data through a slow-light fiber delay-line based on parametric process
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate fine-tuning of a slow-light delay line by propagating 10-Gb/s RZ data packets through a parametric amplifier, and for the first time investigate the system performance of such a delay line.

articleTitle: A novel chromatic dispersion monitoring technique using frequency-modulated and amplitude-modulated pilot tones
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel chromatic dispersion monitoring technique using frequency-modulated and amplitude-modulated pilot tones. Unlike the conventional pilot-tone-based monitoring techniques, the proposed technique could discriminate the sign of accumulated dispersion

articleTitle: 511-chip, 500-chip/s OCDMA en/decoders based on equivalent phase-shift method
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel sampled Bragg gratings without phase shifts are demonstrated for high-quality OCDMA en/decoders with large chip-count. Precise phase control can be realized by only uniform phase mask and fabrication setup with sub-micron precision

articleTitle: Ultrashort-cavity passively mode-locked fiber lasers using carbon nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review our studies on high-repetition rate, ultrashort-cavity mode-locked fiber Fabry-Perot lasers (FFPLs) using Er:Yb fiber and carbon nanotube (CNT) based mode lockers. We also present our recent results of an ultrashort-cavity SOA-based mode-locked laser.

articleTitle: Polarization-independent OTDM demultiplexer based on NOLM with a polarization diversity loop
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Polarization-independent all-optical time-division-demultiplexing is successfully demonstrated by incorporating a polarization diversity loop into the conventional NOLM. The polarization dependence is reduced from 6.3 dB to 0.6 dB in a 40 to 10-Gb/s OTDM experiment.

articleTitle: Flat supercontinuum generation in a dispersion-flattened nonlinear photonic crystal fiber with normal dispersion
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a flat supercontinuum generation over 185 nm in a dispersion-flattened nonlinear photonic crystal fiber working in the normal dispersion regime only, with all-fiber configuration and only 10 mW mode-locked pump pulses.

articleTitle: 2.5 Gbit/s modulation of 1300 nm single-mode photonic crystal VCSELs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Long wavelength single fundamental mode photonic crystal VCSELs have been fabricated and demonstrated to deliver 1 mW of output power up to 90degC. 2.5 Gbit/s modulation experiments show clear and open eyes

articleTitle: A simply tunable optical CDMA encoder/decoder for two-dimensional cyclic permutable codes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a simply tunable optical codec using a cyclic wavelength shifter, which can be applied for two-dimensional optical CDMA (O-CDMA) schemes. The cyclic wavelength shifter is based on dual-band holographic grating. By using this device, it is easy to implement various optical CDMA codecs utilizing constant-weight cyclic-permutable codes. In this paper, the basic principle and the feasibility of the proposed device is demonstrated experimentally.

articleTitle: 40-Gbit/s all-optical header processing for packet routing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate 40-Gbit/s all-optical header processing using two ultrafast nonlinear interferometers to simultaneously forward two packets through a 2&2 spatial switch. Clear, open eye diagrams are observed, indicating low-error-rate forwarding decisions for packet routing.

articleTitle: Development of a sophisticated sub-micro fusion splicer for FTTP applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The installation of Japanese FTTP (fiber to the premise) networks often includes mechanical splices and optical fiber connectors to connect the drop cable to a premise or to connect an indoor cable within a premise. However, fusion splices are still the preferred method of connecting fiber at locations away from the premise. These remote locations include a variety of splicing environments such as aerial splicing that demand equipment portability and versatility.
