For these reasons, an increasing number of customers require an easy to use, smaller, and lighter splicer with a full set of features. To meet these customer requirements, the highest priority when we developed our new fusion splicer was that it would be the smallest, lightest, and most versatile in the industry.

articleTitle: In-service monitoring of chromatic dispersion and polarization mode dispersion for RZ-DPSK signal based asynchronous amplitude histogram evaluation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate an in-service monitoring technique based on asynchronous amplitude histogram evaluation for RZ-DPSK signals that can monitor chromatic dispersion and polarization-mode dispersion simultaneously. The principle of operation was studied and verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Integrated photonic/RF 40-Gb/s burst-mode optical clock recovery for asynchronous optical packet switching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An integrated 40-Gb/s burst-mode optical clock recovery circuit with nanosecond locking time is demonstrated. It has 643-fs RMS jitter. The integrated burst-mode optical clock recovery is also used to detect the envelope of 40-Gb/s RZ payloads with 3-ns rise time.

articleTitle: Optical clock pulse-train generator for asynchronous arbitrary-length optical packet processing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An optical clock pulse-train generator (OCPTG) for processing asynchronous arbitrary-length optical packets with no preamble is developed for the first time. Error-free demultiplexing for 10-Gbit/s asynchronous optical packets is achieved using the OCPTG

articleTitle: Non-uniform spectral encoding of measured mode-locked laser pulses for performance enhancement of optical CDMA networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel non-uniform spectral encoding scheme in a SPECTS O-CDMA system. Simulations incorporating measured mode-locked laser pulse spectrum indicate that enhanced BER performance and 8-fold increase in system capacity are possible

articleTitle: Mitigation of SPM effect by using Manchester code on optical BPSK-SSB transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Tolerance to SPM is evaluated in a dispersion-compensated transmission using optical BPSK single sideband modulation. Optical Manchester code is more tolerant to fiber nonlinearity and less pattern dependency than the NRZ format on BPSK-SSB transmission.

articleTitle: The role of emerging broadband technologies on the converged packet-based network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The vision of network convergence toward a consolidated packet-based network has been discussed for years, though it is still not a reality. Currently, there are numerous overlay networks such as IP, ATM, frame relay (FR), Ethernet, SONET, DWDM and wireless for different services. The evolution pace toward convergence has been slow due to economic, technical and regulatory issues. In this paper, new emerging broadband technologies are discussed. This paper illustrates how those technologies can be integrated together to provide a seamless converged wireline and wireless network and outlines the challenges ahead to make the vision of a packet-based network successful.

articleTitle: Highly reliable (<1000 FITs at 95/spl deg/C) 1.5-/spl mu/m DFB laser high-mesa SIBH structure for CWDM systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have achieved a DFB laser with high reliability (<1000 FlTs) at 95/spl deg/C that is capable of error-free 2.5 Gbps 80 km transmissions at -20 to 100/spl deg/C. Long-term stability has been achieved by suppressing the second stage degradation.

articleTitle: Reducing losses in photonic crystal fibres
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The loss of photonic crystal fibres is determined by the fibre attenuation, and also input and output coupling losses. I will review present understanding of both types of loss, and how they can be mitigated

articleTitle: Novel SOA-based switch for multiple radio-over-fiber service applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An all-optical 3/spl times/3 SOA-based switch is demonstrated for routing radio-over-fiber signals. It is demonstrated that different RF signals, such as terrestrial digital TV and wireless LAN, can be routed simultaneously with a switching guard-band of only 500 ns.

articleTitle: Mitigation of intra-channel nonlinear distortion in 42.7 Gb/s RZ transmission using a single chip optical equalizer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated the mitigation of intra-channel nonlinear distortion in 42.7 Gb/s RZ transmission with 107.5 km amplifier spans without Raman amplification using an optical equalizer, allowing increased transmission distance from 2043 km to 3010 km.

articleTitle: Demonstration of automatic multi-reliability service class LSP provisioning via coordination of GMPLS/OIF-OUNI
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Automatic multi-reliability service class LSP provisioning via coordination of GMPLS/OIF-OUNI protocols is successfully demonstrated for the first time. This paper experimentally evaluates the provisioning and switching performance in a photonic IP network.

articleTitle: Backup reprovisioning after network-state updates in survivable mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate benefits of backup reprovisioning after network-state updates in survivable mesh networks. Our approach achieves good capacity utilization and network robustness. We study tradeoff between capacity optimization and computation/reconfiguration overhead with different reprovisioning periods.

articleTitle: High-speed optical switching of InAlGaAs/InAlAs multi-mode interference photonic switch with partial index-modulation region (MIPS-P)
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A semiconductor multi-mode interference photonic switch with partial index-modulation regions (MIPS-P) was fabricated, and we demonstrated high-speed switching operation in a switching time of about 1.5 ns, for the first time, at a repetition rate of 10 MHz.

articleTitle: Extruded polymer preforms for high-NA polymer microstructured fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report on use of billet extrusion for the first time to fabricate microstructured polymer optical fiber preforms. The shape and relative size of the air holes in the preform is preserved during fiber drawing.

articleTitle: Spectral characteristics of side-polished endlessly single-mode photonic crystal fiber: waveguide dispersion
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate spectral characteristics of side-polished endlessly single-mode photonic crystal fibers by polishing-depth and radius of curvature, which are important to evanescent coupling, waveguide loss, higher-order modes excitation, and dispersion slopes of photonic crystal fiber components.

articleTitle: Router-OXC cooperation for fault recovery employing GMPLS control plane for photonic IX
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes fault recovery procedures to improve the reliability of photonic Internet exchanges and presents experimental results that confirm the feasibility of employing these procedures for the first time. The proposed procedures employ cooperation between routers and optical cross-connects using over-lay model generalized multi-protocol label switching control plane to utilize network resources efficiently.

articleTitle: Ultra-fast differential-phase-shift quantum key distribution using single-photon detectors based on up-conversion in periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We report a differential-phase-shift quantum key distribution experiment in which we employed single photon detectors based on frequency up-conversion in periodically poled lithium niobate waveguides. We achieved a shifted key rate of 1 Mbit/s over 30 km of optical fiber, which is two orders of magnitude larger than the previous record.

articleTitle: Non-intrusive estimation of PMD-induced penalty via high speed, high resolution spectral polarimeter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We developed and tested a non-disruptive technique for estimating PMD-induced system penalties based on spectral polarization measurements. This technique is able to track penalty in milliseconds, and can be scaled to monitor the C-band

articleTitle: Spectral efficient transmission of 40 Gbps per channel over 50 GHz spaced DWDM systems using optical carrier suppression, separation and optical duobinary modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel scheme of transmitting 40-Gb/s/channel over 50-GHz spaced DWDM systems is realized by optical carrier suppression and separation technique and optical duobinary modulation. Through simulation, we evaluate the performance of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: High-density optical burst switched access network combining WDM and TDM over a passive optical infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A high-density burst switched passive access network implementing a highly-optimized WDM/TDM geographic bandwidth allocation protocol is presented. Network simulations have validated the protocol and 2.5 Gb/s multi-wavelength optical transmission tests have demonstrated practical feasibility.

articleTitle: Distributed Brillouin sensor based on Brillouin scattering for structural health monitoring
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We used the distributed Brillouin sensor (DBS) to monitor the structure changes in a steel pipe and a concrete/FRP (fiber reinforced polymer) column subjected to heavy loads. We have shown that the DBS is capable of providing strain distribution of both column and pipe under the various loads at structural and local level for the spatial resolution of 10-15 cm. The DBS can detect deformations, cracks and buckling before they became fatal to the structure. This demonstrates that it is a promising tool for structural health monitoring (SHM).

articleTitle: Orthogonal Polarization Heterodyne OSNR Monitoring Technique Insensitive to Polarization Effects
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A monitoring technique is demonstrated that utilizes polarization orthogonality and heterodyne mixing to measure the in-band optical-signal-to-noise-ratio. This technique is insensitive to PMD and nonlinear polarization scattering, and operates independently of the optical signal properties.

articleTitle: A novel frequency-offset monitoring technique in direct-detection DPSK systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel technique to monitor the frequency offset between the optical signal and delay interferometer in direct-detection DPSK systems. The monitoring range and accuracy of the proposed technique were measured to be /spl plusmn/2 GHz and /spl sim/1 MHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Radial basis function network for non-linear EDC in optical communication OOK system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We introduce the radial basis function network for electronic dispersion compensation in optical communication systems with OOK and a direct detection receiver. The RBF method introduces a non-linear equalization technique suitable for optical communication system

articleTitle: Bidirectional amplification with linear optical amplifier in WDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: To increase the system margin and service coverage in WDM-PON, bidirectional amplification with linear optical amplifier is demonstrated. We measured the sensitivity enhancement of 12.8 dB for downstream and 11.4 dB for upstream channel.

articleTitle: Modeling 40 Gb/s CSRZ-DPSK and RZ-DPSK trans-Atlantic transmission with dispersion slope compensation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We model a 40 Gb/s RZ and CSRZ-DPSK transmission over a trans-Atlantic system using non-slope-matched fiber with dispersion slope compensation. Slope compensation is necessary to achieve reasonable margins.

articleTitle: Theory of adiabatic optical fiber and microfiber tapers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The theory of adiabatic optical fiber tapers is revised with the Landau-Dykhne formula, which provides simple and physically clear expressions for the intermode transmission amplitudes and is used to determine the smallest microfiber diameter enabling light transmission

articleTitle: Polarization-nulling method for monitoring OSNR in WDM network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper reviews the current status of the OSNR monitoring techniques based on the polarization-nulling method. The results show that the polarization-nulling method can be used for monitoring OSNR in a dynamic WDM network and enhance its operation and maintenance

articleTitle: S/C/L-band wavelength conversion by cross-polarization modulation in a dispersion-flattened nonlinear photonic-crystal fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We study the conversion bandwidth of cross-polarization-modulation based wavelength conversion scheme. Both numerical and experimental results show that the conversion bandwidth can be extended to cover S-, C- and L-band for 10 Gb/s non-return-to-zero signals.

articleTitle: Backward Raman amplification in randomly-birefringent and spun fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The vector interaction of a counter-propagating Raman pump and a signal is numerically solved for randomly birefringent spun fibers. High gain enhancement and reduced variance are attained even for large polarization mode dispersion.

articleTitle: Demonstration of an extended reach (425 m) Ethernet system over large core polymer optical fibers for access/edge networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We developed a media-converter and a transceiver for 10 Mb/s Ethernet transmission over 1 mm PMMA step-index polymer optical fibers. Using commercial optoelectronic components and a proprietary protocol, we demonstrate the system over a record distance of 425 meters.

articleTitle: Tuned attenuation efficiency of a silicon photonic variable optical attenuator with supplementary diodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Supplementary diodes were introduced into a silicon photonic variable optical attenuator, formed by 4 forward-biased lateral p-z-n diodes connected in series, in order to tune its attenuation efficiency.

articleTitle: RZ/CSRZ-DPSK signal generation using only Mach-Zehnder modulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a novel scheme to generate return-to-zero/carrier-suppressed return-to-zero differential phase-shift keyed (RZ/CSRZ-DPSK) signal, which needs only one Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM). It is more cost-effective compared to conventional schemes due to its simple configuration

articleTitle: Noise statistics of fiber optical parametric amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We show both theoretically and experimentally that the probability density function of a signal amplified by parametric amplifiers with pump excess noise is non-Gaussian and asymmetric. This impacts the relationship between the noise figure and the bit-error rate.

articleTitle: Effect of nonlinearities on PMD system degradations
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We review and discuss cross-phase modulation-induced polarization state changes in WDM systems, so called cross-polarization modulation, XPolM, and how it influences outage probabilities in polarization mode dispersion-limited systems.

articleTitle: Higher bit rates for quasi-linear optical data transmission systems via constrained coding
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Application of constrained coding to 40-Gb/s dispersion-managed optical communication systems limited by intrachannel four-wave mixing is considered. When transmitted sequences obey the so-called (2, /spl infin/) constraint, a 50% increase in data rate is demonstrated.

articleTitle: OTDR technique for characterization of fiber optic parametric amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel technique for characterization of power evolution in fiber optic parametric amplifiers based on optical time domain reflectometry is presented. The technique is suitable for analyzing the exponential gain along the amplifying fiber

articleTitle: Secure stealth transmission over an existing public fiber-optical network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We develop a spread-spectrum based approach to secure communications over existing public fiber-optical networks. The secure channel is hidden under the noise floor of the network thus allowing cryptographic and steganographic security capabilities.

articleTitle: Microsecond optical burst add-drop multiplexing WDM ring networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate experimentally an OB-ADM node for WDM ring network applications. Burst identifiers control add/drop multiplexing of 10- to 100-/spl mu/sec optical data bursts. Optical burst amplification and transmission at 9.953 Gbit/s are implemented in a 3-node testbed.

articleTitle: Modulation parameter tolerance for 8- and 16-APSK (amplitude- and phase-shift keying) signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the impact of non-ideal modulating condition on multilevel APSK modulations, and find 4-% angular misalignment of orthogonal PSK components or residual chirp of 0.2 in ASK modulator causes 1-dB penalty of PSK components

articleTitle: Engineering and planning tool for an ultra-long-haul optical mesh transport system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a software application that optimizes network and traffic design; provides operations, verification, and diagnostic support capabilities; and enhances cost-effectiveness for LambdaXtreme/sup /spl trade// transport - an ultra-long-haul optical mesh transport system developed by Lucent Technologies.

articleTitle: Congestion control scheme in optical packet switched networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a congestion control scheme for optical packet switched networks, for use with edge smoothing and reduced core optical buffers. Simulation results indicate that it interacts favourably with TCP's congestion control mechanism.

articleTitle: Tunability of the gain spectrum in an erbium-doped fiber with depressed-cladding
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The bending losses of a depressed-cladding erbium-doped fiber have been exploited to tune the fiber amplifier gain in the wavelength range between the S-band and the C-band

articleTitle: 10 GHz actively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber ring laser using electro-absorption modulator and a linear optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a 10-GHz actively mode-locked erbium-doped fiber laser that incorporates an electro-absorption modulator and a linear optical amplifier. Stable pulses with peak power of 120 mW and pulsewidth of 2.4 ps are obtained.

articleTitle: Using FEC code for improving the WDM/SCM - PON performance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For improving the performance of the most cost-efficient WDM/SCM-PON, the way how to choose a FEC code is described. The choosing methods are a code rate and hard resource size. A RS code is best suitable.

articleTitle: Design of Raman-based NOLM for optical 2R regeneration of RZ-DPSK transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a concept for all-optical differential phase-shift keying (DPSK) signal regeneration, based on a new design of Raman amplified nonlinear loop mirror (RA-NOLM). We demonstrate simultaneous amplitude-shape regeneration and phase noise reduction in high-speed DPSK systems by use of the RA-NOLM combined with spectral filtering.

articleTitle: Fast residual chromatic dispersion monitoring for dynamic burst networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents experimental results of a novel method for residual dispersion monitoring in 40 Gbit/s systems. The measurement time of this implementation is in the order of 10 mus, making this scheme applicable to dynamically reconfigurable burst networks

articleTitle: General approach to hitless switching and FSR extension resonators in integrated photonic circuits
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A hitless bypass switch for microphotonic channel add-drop filters that is based on /spl Delta//spl beta/ switches is described. We generalize the design to a large class of devices enabling variants of the switch and application to free-spectral-range extension in tunable filters.

articleTitle: Protection capacity savings due to end-to-end shared backup path restoration in optical mesh networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: It is well known that for link-restoration in an optical mesh network, the lower bound on the ratio between protection capacity and working capacity is 1/(d-1) where d is the average node degree of the mesh topology. No similar bounds are known for shared backup path restoration in which backup paths share bandwidth on their links if their primary paths are link disjoint. Shared backup path restoration has recently received interest and is being deployed by carriers because of its reduced restoration capacity overhead. This paper presents a quantitative analytical model for the protection capacity requirement in an optical mesh networks with an end-to-end shared backup path based restoration scheme. This analytical model can be used for quick back-of-the-envelope calculations of restoration capacity overhead without explicit computation-intensive routing of primary and shared backup paths. We perform simulations of the efficiency of network utilization of path-based restoration, and in particular focus on the impact of sharing of wavelength channels for mesh-restored lightpaths. We also investigate the impact of sharing of wavelength channels for mesh-restored lightpaths on the increase in restoration latency, since cross-connects are soft-reserved during provisioning and need to be setup on the backup path after failure.

articleTitle: Single-step fabrication of raised index X-couplers via direct UV writing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: X-couplers having low polarization and wavelength dependency with 1.9-95% coupling ratios were fabricated in a single step via direct UV writing, exhibiting typical excess loss of 1.0 dB. First experimental validation of analytical and BPM modeling is also presented

articleTitle: Chromatic dispersion monitoring using synchronous sampling
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate that by synchronously sampling on both sides of the eye diagram, group velocity dispersion of up to 1800 ps/nm can be accurately assessed. The effect of noise and self phase modulation on the accuracy is also investigated.

articleTitle: Advances and limitations in the modeling of fabricated photonic bandgap fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We model fabricated silica photonic bandgap fibers and achieve good agreement between simulated and measured properties. We identify the size of the SEM bitmap image as the ultimate limit to the accurate calculation of surfaces modes within the bandgap

articleTitle: 4/spl times/4 high-speed switching subsystem with VOA (< 10 /spl mu/s) using PLZT beam-deflector for optical burst switching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We developed a 4times4 high-speed optical switch subsystem with variable optical attenuation (VOA). This switch subsystem allows high-speed level adjustment as well as high-speed switching by using the electro-optic (EO) effect of PLZT. We demonstrate 5.5-mus switching with VOA to obtain the desired output power for optical burst switching (OBS)

articleTitle: Integrated optical label read and payload envelope detection circuit for optical label swapping
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate the first integrated 10 Gbps optical label recovery and 40 Gbps optical payload envelope detector circuit. Error free optical label recovery, nanosecond payload envelope detection, and optical label swapping are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Toward transmission applications with microstructured fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recent progress of microstructured fibers for optical transmission has been described. We demonstrate potentiality of the fiber for future ultra high capacity optical transmission systems, which are not realized with a conventional single-mode fiber

articleTitle: Highly efficient, wavelength-selective out-coupling of cladding mode using tilted fiber grating and micro-etched cladding
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A highly efficient, wavelength-selective detection through micro-etched groove on cladding of tilted fiber gratings (TFGs) is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. More than 88% power of the cladding mode is out-coupled into an optical power detector.

articleTitle: Evolving a fibre-to-the-node access infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Competition between the Cablecos and Telcos in Canada to win the broadband home is intense. Cablecos are already delivering voice services. Erosion of the Telco voice market is being evidenced. For Bell Canada, delivery of a broadcast video service is a critical component in winning the broadband home. Bell Canada is already an entrenched national satellite video service provider. Nevertheless, a wireline video delivery solution is essential to complement satellite and increase market share in major urban areas. Bell Canada is deploying a fibre-to-the-node infrastructure in existing residential areas for delivery of IP-based broadcast video content. Fibre-to-the-Node fully leverages the copper distribution plant enabling broad coverage and rapid revenue generation. Emerging VDSL2 technology delivers throughputs of 25 Mbps to the end customer over this infrastructure. However, delivery of the full set of competitive services including multiple high definition video streams and on demand content stresses this architecture. An evolution strategy is required. This paper compares the evolution alternatives including fibre-to-the-premises. Emphasis is on planning considerations enabling a cost-effective evolution to a fibre-to-the-premises architecture.

articleTitle: Engineering methodology for the use of SOAs and CWDM transmission in the metro network environment
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We investigate the OSNR performance of cascaded SOAs in CWDM metropolitan networks. SOA PDG and noise-figure requirements are determined by an engineering methodology based on careful receiver characterization. Performance is compared to conventional EDFA-amplified DWDM.

articleTitle: The impact of gating timing jitter on a 160 Gb/s demultiplexer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The impact of gating timing jitter on a 160 Gb/s demultiplexer is investigated by using two pulse sources with different timing jitter properties. It is found that jitter in the range 20 kHz-10 MHz is essential to minimize.

articleTitle: A fast and reliable algorithm for electronic pre-equalization of SPM and chromatic dispersion
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a fast algorithm to compute the pre-equalized waveform for simultaneous compensation of the self-phase modulation and chromatic-dispersion experienced by a 10-Gb/s optical signal, and show its robustness against inaccurate knowledge on transmission link details.

articleTitle: A "black-link" approach for sharing optical fiber infrastructure and enabling multi-services
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An innovative optical infrastructure sharing solution for triple play services is described. A "black-link" type of architecture is proposed. We finish by outlining the benefits both commercially and architecturally delivered by this new model.

articleTitle: Improving vulnerability of shared-path protection subject to double-link failures
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In shared-path protection for 100% single-link failures recovery, the first link failure will leave many links vulnerable to the second link failure. We propose and evaluate different policies to improve the network vulnerability.

articleTitle: Narrowband 2/spl times/10 Gbit/s quaternary intensity modulation based on duobinary modulation in two polarizations with unequal amplitudes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Two duobinary 10 Gbit/s data streams with orthogonal polarizations and unequal amplitudes allow to generate a narrowband 20 Gbit/s quaternary intensity modulation. Sensitivity and CD tolerance of this generation scheme are -17.6 dBm and 530 ps/nm, respectively

articleTitle: Low-density parity-check codes for 40 Gb/s transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: BER performance of LDPC codes, generalized LDPC codes and nonbinary LDPC codes, suitable for 40 Gb/s transmission, are compared against turbo product codes and RS concatenation schemes.

articleTitle: Simultaneous all-optical inverted and non-inverted wavelength conversion using a single-stage fiber optical parametric amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have demonstrated, for the first time to our knowledge, simultaneous all-optical inverted and non-inverted wavelength conversion by using a single-stage two-pump fiber optical parametric amplifier with extinction ratio between 7 and 14 dB over 24 nm.

articleTitle: Fiber Bragg grating based dispersion compensator slope-matched for LEAF fiber
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A dispersion compensator matching the spectrally-varying dispersion of LEAF fiber is presented, based on a multi-channel fiber Bragg grating that operates over the full C-band

articleTitle: A practical traffic grooming scheme in all-optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper, we propose and evaluate a new concept of traffic aggregation in mesh networks that aims to alleviate both the bandwidth underutilization and scalability concerns typical of all-optical wavelength routed networks

articleTitle: Helium implanted silicon waveguide photodetectors for optical power monitors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The enhanced photo-response of helium ion implanted silicon waveguides as a function of different anneal temperatures and durations is reported. The enhancement in responsivity at communication wavelength was sufficient for use as optical power monitors.

articleTitle: Experimental study comparing characteristics of 10-Gb/s RZ-AMI formats generated by CML and MZM-DI transmitters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare the dispersion and nonlinear tolerance of 10-Gb/s RZ-AMI format generated by a chirp managed laser (CML) with that generated by a MZM delay-interferometer transmitter. The CML delivers comparable performance in a small footprint.

articleTitle: Least squares procedure for measuring Mueller matrices
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A least squares method is presented that allows the Mueller matrix of an optical fiber to be determined with high accuracy from measurements of the output Stokes vector for different unknown input polarization states

articleTitle: Gradient-method based adaptive control of tunable dispersion compensator that minimizes time-domain waveform error
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel technique to control tunable dispersion compensator adaptively. This technique is required for realizing high-speed all optical routing networks. Numerical simulation results show that the technique compensates the dispersion quickly and effectively

articleTitle: Large-capacity hybrid WDM/SCMA-PON using wavelength-locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a hybrid WDM/SCMA-PON for a large capacity access network. Using FEC technique, we can share 3 or possibly more subchannels of 125 Mb/s data within an optical channel of 100 GHz-spaced wavelength router.

articleTitle: Comparative study of spectrum-sliced incoherent light systems employing SOA-based noise suppression
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We compare three SOA-based noise suppression approaches employed in spectrum-sliced WDM systems. Although the SOA at the transmitter provides best noise suppression, the SOA at the receiver may provide better value in last-mile access applications.

articleTitle: A design criterion for cleavage-robust microstructured fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Cleavage patterns of high air-fraction, double-clad microstructured fibers (MSFs) are analyzed using fracture mechanics. Critical fracture depth is shown to be a measure explaining the different patterns and is proposed as a criterion to design cleavage-robust MSFs.

articleTitle: Optimizing operating conditions to reduce data pattern dependence induced by slow light elements
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We analyze pattern dependence induced by slow light and define figure of merit involving pulse delay and data degradation to optimize slow-light elements. The pattern dependence can be reduced, with up to 5 dB Q improvement, by detuning slow-light devices

articleTitle: Line optimization in long-haul transmission systems with 42.8-Gbit/s RZ-DQPSK modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We discuss dispersion and power map optimization for 42.8-Gbit/s RZ-DQPSK DWDM transmission over standard-single-mode-fiber with terrestrial length fiber spans. We experimentally show that long-haul 42.8-Gbit/s RZ-DQPSK transmission is feasible with high tolerances towards deviations in the dispersion map.

articleTitle: Electrical dispersion compensation for different modulation formats with optical filtering
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present electrical dispersion compensation by using maximum-likelihood-sequence-estimation (MLSE) and decision-feedback-equalization for different modulation formats. Especially, MLSE performance with strong optical filtering is investigated.

articleTitle: Cascadability and wavelength tunability assessment of a 2R regeneration device based on saturable absorber and semiconductor optical amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We assess a new 2R regenerator based on a microcavity saturable absorber and SOA combination in a 10 Gbit/s two path, recirculating loop. The device, whose location impact is studied, is tunable over 13 nm

articleTitle: Four-degree hub switch module using multi-chip planar lightwave circuit integration technology for transparent ROADM ring interconnection
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have developed a PLC-based 32-wavelength 4-degree hub switch module, which consists of a broadcast coupler with a demultiplexer for local-drop, and a WSS with wavelength specific ports for local-add. The module size is 220/spl times/135/spl times/14 mm. The insertion loss of the express path in the WSS is 10.8 dB.

articleTitle: Improved Margin in Long-Haul 40 Gb/s Systems Using Bit-Synchronously Modulated RZ-DQPSK
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated a substantial improvement in FEC margin at 40 Gb/s using bit-synchronously modulated RZ-DQPSK. We transmitted 28×40 Gb/s CRZ-DQPSK channels over 6,550 km with ~2 dB of actual FEC margin, without any PMD compensation.

articleTitle: Novel passive free space compact CWDM technology for outdoor applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Recently CWDM system has emerged into one important platform for optical networks. Its low cost configuration helps the WDM technology applying into new applications such as access and FTTX networks, which are very sensitive to cost structure and cost efficiency. This brings additional challenges to the optical components for more different operation conditions. We introduce here a novel compact CWDM module for demultiplexer or multiplexer that has extremely low insertion loss and can work for outdoor applications. With unique technologies of thin film coatings and compact no-shift packaging, the premium performances are achieved with the savings on cost as well. The total loss of a 8-channel module is only 0.7 dB within the passband of /spl plusmn/7.5 nm, together with the PDL of 0.1 dB. The compact CWDM module is proven to be a low cost solution for metro, access, FTTX, CATV head end/node, and wireless networks.

articleTitle: A simple high-speed WDM PON utilizing a centralized supercontinuum broadband light source for colorless ONUs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a simple high-speed WDM-PON, using a centralized supercontinuum broadband light source based on a nonlinear PCF for upstream optical carriers. "Colorless" ONU operation has been demonstrated in a 10 Gb/s bidirectional transmission over 40 km distance

articleTitle: Sensing an optical fiber surface by a microfiber with angstrom accuracy
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: By monitoring the whispering gallery mode resonances, which are excited in an optical fiber by a moving microfiber, we determine the optical fiber effective diameter variation with angstrom accuracy and sensor the residuals and defects on the fiber surface

articleTitle: IRIS: optical switching technologies for scalable data networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical switching technologies developed under the IRIS program will allow scaling of packet routers by two orders of magnitudes and will enable very efficient access networks.

articleTitle: Specification and operation of 160 Gbit/s/port interface optical packet switch prototype with narrow-band optical code label processor and high extinction ratio optical buffer
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have achieved error-free 160 Gbit/s/port optical packet switching (OPS) operation with real packet BERs of less than 10/sup -10/ by OPS prototype based on 25 Gchip/s narrow-band optical code label processor and optical buffers with noise reduction function.

articleTitle: Today's optical network research infrastructures for E-science applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Some of today's scientific discoveries (E-science) involving both compute intensive and data intensive applications require collaboration on a global scale and high capacity optical infrastructures. This talk will discuss some of the optical networking challenges.

articleTitle: Maintaining availability in an optical backbone network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a way to calculate the availability of an optical backbone network and how to control and design availability of specific routes. The two parameters that the carrier can control are the architecture and the 'mean time to repair' (MTTR). To achieve targeted MTTRs, local spares warehouses (LSWs) are distributed throughout the network. This paper presents an innovative method for the optimal placement of LSWs and describes optimal spares storage and replacement policies.

articleTitle: Modelling of WDM terrestrial and submarine links for the design of WDM networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Summary form only for tutorial. This paper is a powerpoint presentation of wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) network design by modelling WDM terrestrial and submarine links. It presents some examples where theoretical tools have been fruitful at 40 Gbit/s as well as for dispersion management at 10 Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Raman crosstalk control in passive optical networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present a new solution to the Raman coupling problem in PON systems carrying sub-carrier modulated analog video. This is done by shaping the spectrum of the digital signals while maintaining the line signal format.

articleTitle: Limits of maximum-likelihood sequence estimation in chromatic dispersion limited systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We experimentally investigated the performance of MLSE in chromatic dispersion-limited 10 Gb/s links, and assessed the limits in terms of the number of states and A/D converter sample rate, up to 40 GSa/s

articleTitle: 10-Gbps 1.3 and 1.55-μm InP-based VCSELs: 85 ° C 10-km Error-free Transmission and Room Temperature 40-km Transmission at 1.55-μm with EDC
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: 10-Gbps Error-free transmission through 10-km single-mode fiber by both 1.3 and 1.55-μm AlGaInAs/InP VCSELs have been demonstrated at 85°C. Also, 1.55-μm VCSELs with EDC shows 4-times distance expansion (40-km) for 10.7-Gbps FEC format over standard single-mode fiber.

articleTitle: PIN photodiode modules for 80 Gbit/s and beyond
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The paper reports key characteristics of recent developments in the field of broadband photodetectors for 1.55 mum wavelength. A 100 Gbit/s photodetector module and a balanced photodetector for direct detection of 80 Gbit/s DPSK transmission formats are presented

articleTitle: Label-based path switching and error-free forwarding in a prototype optical burst switching node using a fast 4/spl times/4 optical switch and shared wavelength conversion
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate for the first time optical burst switching using fast and scalable EO switch and a shared wavelength converter for contention resolution. 3.5 /spl mu/m label routing of variable-length bursts and error-free operation was achieved at 10 Gbps payload.

articleTitle: Full-duplex 1 Gbps 60 GHz-band radio-on-fiber access based on loop-back optical heterodyne technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In the system proposed herein, uplink and downlink share the optical-signal-generation module in the central station and electro-absorption modulators in the base stations without interfering with each other, which simplifies the system architecture significantly.

articleTitle: High-performance InP-based optical modulators
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate two types of high-speed semiconductor optical modulators operating at 40 Gbit/s with reduced driving voltage. One is a compact Mach-Zehnder modulator module that achieves error-free operation in a push-pull configuration with a peak-to-peak voltage of 1.3 V. The other is an electroabsorption modulator integrated with microwave coplanar waveguides and driven by a voltage as low as 0.79 V

articleTitle: High sensitivity all-optical sampling for 40 Gb/s signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: High sensitivity and absence of impedance mismatching makes optical sampling techniques attractive for monitoring 40 Gb/s signals. We present theory and experiments showing 40 Gb/s eye-diagrams with 20 dB SNR at -25 dBm average signal power.

articleTitle: Field Trial of 3-WDM × 10-OCDMA × 10.71 Gbps, Truly-asynchronous, WDM/DPSK-OCDMA Using Hybrid E/D Without FEC and Optical Threshold
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A cost-effective WDM/DPSK-OCDMA sharing a single multi-port encoder in central office, tunable decoders in ONU was demonstrated in field trial. 111 km error-free transmission of truly-asynchronous, 3-WDM×l0-OCDMA×l0.71Gbps/user has been achieved without FEC and optical thresholding.

articleTitle: Tunable Narrowband Optical Filter in CMOS
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate a compact, fully tunable, narrowband (1GHz) 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>order pole/zero optical filter that is fabricated in a silicon complementary metal oxide semiconductor foundry.

articleTitle: A ROF downstream link with optical mm-wave generation using optical phase modulator for providing broadband optical-wireless access service
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have experimentally demonstrated a ROF downstream link with optical mm-wave generation using optical phase modulator and optical filtering for providing broadband optical-wireless access service for the first time. We extend the transmission distance limited by fiber dispersion using a novel scheme.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a novel all-optical multilevel 4-amplitude-shifted-keying coding/decoding scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrated for the first time an all-optical multilevel 4-amplitude-shifted-keying coding and decoding technique, which encodes two on-off-keying signals into a 4-ASK signal using cross absorption modulation in an electro-absorption modulator and employs fiber-based all-optical approach to facilitate data detection.

articleTitle: 10.7 Gb/s CWDM system transmission with 8 channels 140 nm bandwidth over 120 km using two SOAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate 8-channel CWDM transmission at 10.7 Gb/s over 120 km of fiber in two different configurations using just two SOAs for wide bandwidth amplification. The total system capacity-distance product is 9.6 Tb/s-km.

articleTitle: Measurement of passive optical components using a carrier and single sideband
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple method based on arbitrary optical signal generation is presented for measuring the magnitude and phase of the transfer function of passive optical components. The method offers fine resolution along the frequency axis as well as a simple setup.

articleTitle: Inter-channel crosstalk cancellation by encoding with adjacent channels in coherent WDM
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A pre-compensation technique for inter-channel crosstalk cancellation in a dense WDM system is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. Waveform distortion caused by inter-channel crosstalk is canceled out at receiver by encoding each channel using its own data and its adjacent data.

articleTitle: New intradyne receiver with electronic-driven phase and polarization diversity
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A novel PSK receiver technique is proposed based on electronic-driven diversity, without optical hybrid and polarization beam splitters. It achieves high tolerance to phase noise and feasible implementation with commercial lasers

articleTitle: Relationship between the achievable distance of WDM transmission systems and criterion of quality for DCM
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a simple analytical expression to connect the formerly presented criterion of quality for dispersion compensated modules with the achievable distance of optical systems and extrapolate on performance brought by existing and future modules

articleTitle: Optical minimum-shift keying format and its dispersion tolerance
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Detailed principle for optical MSK generation and detection is presented. 10.7 Gb/s MSK data is transmitted and its dispersion tolerance is compared with that of RZ-DPSK and RZ-OOK. Results show that MSK exhibits better tolerance than other two formats.

articleTitle: New Field Trial Distance Record of 3040 km on Wide Reach WDM with 10 and 40 Gbps Transmission Including OC-768 Traffic Without Regeneration
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Verizon successfully carried Juniper OC-768 traffic on their Richardson, Texas, field trial network to 3040km and 2560km, respectively, using Mintera's 40Gbps RZ-DPSK and CS-RZ transponders over Xtera's all Raman ULH system loaded with 68×l0Gbps channels.

articleTitle: Burst mode 10 Gbps optical header recovery and lookup processing for asynchronous variable-length 40 Gbps optical packet switching
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate 10 Gbps asynchronous optical header recovery with less than 20 bits lock time and over 380 bits hold time after the label end. Layer-1(BER) and Layer-2(Header Loss) results are presented for the first time

articleTitle: A wavelength switching operation of a Si-waveguide asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer having a ferro-electric liquid crystal cladding
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We proposed and fabricated a novel optical switching device using a Si-waveguide asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer with a ferro-electric liquid crystal cladding. We demonstrated the wavelength switching operation with the experimental device fabricated at 1550 nm wavelength.

articleTitle: 1.6-b/s/Hz Spectrally Efficient 40 × 85.6-Gb/s Transmission Over 1,700 km of SSMF Using POLMUX-RZ-DQPSK
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Long-haul transmission (>1,000 km) with 1.6-b/s/Hz spectral efficiency is shown for the first time. Using polarization-multiplexed RZ-DQPSK, we demonstrate 40 × 85.6-Gb/s transmission over 1,700 km (18 × 94.5 km) of standard-single-mode fiber with 1-dB Q-margin.

articleTitle: High-density optical wiring technologies for optical backplane interconnection using downsized fibers and pre-installed fiber type multi optical connectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We have developed a high-/spl Delta/ downsized MMF that can withstand bending and a multi-fiber MT connector that allows on-site installation without polishing, as optical wiring technologies for achieving high-density optical backplane interconnection within such devices.

articleTitle: Physical network configuration of next generation home network
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The next generation home network (NgHN) uses the optical fiber for broadband communication with QoS (quality of service). The physical network configuration should be optimized considering total cable length, scalability, and reliability. Star and ring topologies are compared in terms of cable length; with or without hub and with a ring or multiple rings. These comparisons are based on a generalized house model. Expected future services for the NgHN and their requirements are also described and discussed.

articleTitle: Carrier class Ethernet service delivery migrating SONET to IP & triple play offerings
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The general service provider network infrastructure consists of a huge installed base of SONET. While providing high reliability and availability of services, SONET is inefficient when provisioning data. These inefficiencies are exacerbated as service demand becomes more packet-based. E-line point-to-point and E-LAN multipoint services are in demand by businesses in the financial, retail, medical, media and other industries due to their low cost, ease-of-use, scalability and manageability. To maintain high levels of performance and availability, the service provider network will need to monitor end-to-end performance, remotely troubleshoot the network, and efficiently transport Ethernet traffic. It is cost prohibitive to build a completely new network, and an IP-based network lacks the resiliency of a SONET network. The win-win approach is to maintain the SONET attributes of resiliency, performance monitoring and operations, administration & maintenance (OA&M), but process payloads in a packet-based format instead of in a time division multiplexing (TDM) format. Next-generation SONET technologies such as generic framing procedure (GFP), virtual concatenation (VCAT) and link capacity adjustment scheme (ECAS) were developed for Ethernet service provisioning over SONET (EoS). These EoS capabilities insert Ethernet packets into SONET payloads with some bandwidth efficiencies, but still use TDM for aggregation and transport over the ring. EoS lacks the bandwidth efficiencies needed to adjust for data applications, thereby dedicating bandwidth on the entire SONET ring for each circuit. Resilient packet ring (RPR) converges SONET performance and survivability with efficient processing of packet traffic. RPR addresses the inefficiencies of EoS by implementing bandwidth sharing, spatial reuse and statistical multiplexing. The result of using RPR over SONET instead of EoS is the consumption of significantly less bandwidth and fiber for a given application and the elimination of external Ethernet switches for packet aggregation. For triple play applications, data, voice and video will be packet-based. The network edge to access segment will mainly use gigabit Ethernet (GigE). Initially, the GigE pipe will transport video programming and data for Internet access. Plain old telephone service (POTS) will be transported separately through the network until voice over IP (VoIP) is deployed. The video component will consist of high definition (HD) and standard definition (SD) streams using a payload of about 20 Mbps per subscriber. Best effort data will be about 5 Mbps. This total payload will yield an 80%/20% video/data mix respectively over the GigE circuit. RPR over SONET offers the class of service and bandwidth efficiency capabilities to effectively process the data, voice and video streams of triple play services. This paper show how a service provider can migrate a purely SONET-based network to one offering packet services, while maintaining performance, survivability and efficiently processing packet data. Examples show the differences in bandwidth, fiber and equipment utilization of SONET versus EoS versus RPR over SONET for carrier-class Ethernet and triple play services.

articleTitle: Demultiplexing 160/320 Gb/s to 40 Gb/s using a single SOA assisted by an optical filter
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Error-free demultiplexing of 40-Gb/s base-rate channels out of a 160-Gb/s OTDM signal is achieved using a single SOA and an optical filter. Performance of demultiplexing 320 Gb/s using this technique is also presented.

articleTitle: Field Trial of Signaling Interworking of Multi-carrier ASON/GMPLS Network Domains
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A seamless end-to-end call set up over multi-carrier ASON and GMPLS network domains was successfully achieved. Interworking of two ASON network domains and five GMPLS network domains was demonstrated on a nationwide scale.

articleTitle: Polymer fibre Bragg gratings tunable laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Tunable laser using a polymer fibre Bragg grating with simple axial tension as tuning method is constructed. Continuous tunable wavelength over 35 nm with the peak power around -5 dBm and signal to noise ratio greater than 45 dB has been achieved.

articleTitle: TCP performance experiment on OBS network testbed
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: The TCP performance over OBS is experimentally investigated on OBS testbed. Experimental results show that TCP performance over OBS can be guaranteed in the case of 0.1% burst loss probabilities.

articleTitle: Burst cloning with load balancing
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Burst cloning can reduce the burst blocking probability in an OBS network. With our proposed burst cloning with load balancing (BCLB) scheme, a further reduction of at least 10%, up to 55%, can be achieved.

articleTitle: Fairness of downstream TCP throughput among diversely located ONUs in a GE-PON system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A method for providing fairness of the downstream TCP throughput among diversely located ONUs in a GE-PON system has been proposed and has been successfully demonstrated by using a GE-PON with 32 ONUs placed at 2 km and 50 km.

articleTitle: Compact, Low Cost Chip Scale Triplexer WDM Filters
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A high-index contrast PLC branching delay line filter realizes WDM filters for FTTP triplexer applications. The filters achieve low loss and high extinction ratios, while the ultra-compact dimensions of 1mm × 4mm accommodates thousands of chips a 6" silicon wafer.

articleTitle: Generation of 16-Gb/s MSK signal using a single 10-GHz SSB modulator and simplified encoder/decoder
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a new scheme for generating optical MSK by using a commercial SSB modulator. The demodulation of the signal is based on a 2-bit delay MZI to simplify pre-coding/decoding circuits. This scheme is successfully demonstrated in a 16-Gb/s system.

articleTitle: Burst mode operation of a DS-DBR widely tunable laser for wavelength agile system applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel measurements of signal Q-factor as function of time across an optical burst and implementation of fast control system, giving 3 orders of magnitude switching speed and 5 fold stability improvements on previous DS-DBR measurements, are described.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s transmission over 300 m OM3 fiber from 990-1080 nm with electronic dispersion compensation
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate numerically and experimentally the transmission of 10 Gb/s over OM3 fibers up to 300 m, under low-cost VCSEL launch conditions from 990-1080 nm with electronic dispersion compensation (EDC), showing a path to low cost 40 Gbps links.

articleTitle: Optical MEMS: boom, bust and beyond
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Optical telecommunications bandwidth, spurred by the growth of the Internet, experienced unprecedented growth in the late 1990's. The creation of new enterprises was vast and the expansion of established component, system and services companies was also breathtaking. This period of speculative growth was followed in 2001-2004 by one of the most significant market crashes in history. While $20B of venture capital was invested in optical telecom in the last 10 years, the vast majority of that was lost in recent years. With this, many start-up company who experienced unprecedented growth inaugurated with great fanfare at the end of the 20/sup th/ century were unceremoniously shut down at the start of the 21st. As in all speculative bubbles, innovative technologies were born and buried. Nonetheless, new capabilities emerge from the chaos and disruption; one such example is the advent of optical MEMS (MOEMS). Its development was vigorously pursued in both academic and corporate laboratories during the boom and, in the author's view; MOEMS constitutes a powerful and versatile tool set that is an invaluable residual of the last few years. In telecommunications, MOEMS has proven to be the technology of choice for many optical switching and wavelength management applications. Variable optical attenuators (VOA), wavelength blockers (WB), dynamic gain equalizers (DGE), and most recently wavelength selective switches (WSS) are being used in the numerous recent network deployments. Moreover, agile networks of the future will have MOEMS at every node. This presentation will provide an overview of the history of MOEMS in Telecommunications, discuss its byproducts and project the future of the technology.

articleTitle: Cooperation method considering wavelength assignment and routing problem in optical burst switched networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper presents the cooperation method, which cooperatively deals with RWA problem in distributed optical burst switched networks. The simulation results show that this method improves the burst loss probability

articleTitle: Novel optical packet switched access network architecture
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper describes gigabit Ethernet optical switched access network (GE-OSAN) architecture with non-buffered 1xn optical packet switches. It clarifies the role of the key network element, 1xn optical switching module, in realizing the proposed architecture.

articleTitle: Inelastic strain birefringence in optical fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Retardation data captured by polarimetric stress-measurements in optical fibers have been reinterpreted in terms of both stress and inelastic strain. The linear dependence of strain birefringence on fiber drawing tension defines the Kohlrausch-Williams-Watt exponent

articleTitle: Reconfigurable all-optical logic gate based on a single SOA with improved dynamics
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A simple, compact, ultra-fast, reconfigurable photonic logic gate is demonstrated exploiting four-wave-mixing and cross-gain-modulation in a single semiconductor-optical-amplifier with improved dynamics. Bit-error-rate measurements are reported for XNOR, AND, NOR, and NOT logic functions

articleTitle: Security issues on spectral-phase-encoded optical CDMA with phase-masking scheme
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper proposes a time-varying phase-masking scheme for OCDMA security enhancement. We provide a quantitative analysis of its confidentiality. Analytical results indicate that the phase-masking scheme increases the difficulty of interception and achieves low data interception rates.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of an Interference-Avoidance-Based Protocol for O-CDMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference

articleTitle: Electronic Dispersion Compensation for Enhanced Optical Transmission
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Electronic dispersion compensation by analog and digital equalizers enable a considerable increase of high bit rate optical transmission system tolerances. Electronic equalizers are small size and low power consumption subsystems suitable for compact transponder integration.

articleTitle: Bending and connection loss measurement of PON branching fibers with individually assigned Brillouin frequency shifts
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: This paper describes the bending and connection loss measurement of PON branching fibers with individual Brillouin frequency shifts and the measurement of the peak spectrum of the Brillouin frequency shifts distributed in test fibers

articleTitle: Resilient single-fiber ring access network using coupler-based OADMs and RSOA-based ONUs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: An extended PON access network based on a central single-fiber ring and secondary trees is presented and experimentally demonstrated. The architecture provides resilience and load balancing mechanisms that are totally transparent to the end users.

articleTitle: Shared-wavelength WDM-PON access network for supporting downstream traffic with QoS
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose a novel shared-wavelength WDM-PON architecture to accommodate downstream bursty traffic, and provide architectural support for different QoS to users. Downstream wavelength-allocation algorithm is proposed and its properties are evaluated.

articleTitle: iOPEN: integrated optical Ethernet network for efficient dynamically reconfigurable service provisioning
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We present iOPEN network architecture in metro Ethernet networks to support dynamic reconfiguration of lightpaths between Ethernet switches. The network control and operation algorithms are discussed and simulation results from simple network configuration are presented.

articleTitle: All-optical phase and amplitude regeneration of DPSK signals based on phase-sensitive amplification
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: All-optical regeneration of differential phase-shift keyed signals by an interferometric phase-sensitive amplifier is described theoretically and demonstrated experimentally. Measurements reveal simultaneous reduction of both phase and amplitude noise when the device functions as a limiting amplifier.

articleTitle: Network design and cost analysis of optical VPNs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We define three different ways of measuring the cost of providing circuit-based (e.g., optical) VPN services. We give algorithms for computing these cost measures, and compare them empirically on a Tier I service provider's network.

articleTitle: Single polarization fibers and applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Single polarization fibers are designed so that one polarization propagates, while the other is cut off. Several classes of index profiles can be used. Applications include new transmission systems, sensors, and components

articleTitle: Contention avoidance by composite slot assembling
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We propose composite slot assembling as a software scheme to avoid contention in contention-based time-slotted optical networks. This scheme can be used in edge switches of optical networks supporting multiple-class traffic.

articleTitle: 60 GHz radio-on-fiber downlink systems using optically injection-locked self-oscillating optoelectronic mixers based on InP/InGaAs HPTs
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A 30 GHz hybrid-type optically injection-locked self-oscillating optoelectronic mixer is implemented with a high-performance InP/InGaAs heterojunction photo-transistor. Using this mixer as a harmonic up-converter, 60 GHz radio-on-fiber downlink transmission of 20 Mbps 16QAM data is successfully demonstrated. The link performance is uniform over a wide range of optical LO powers.

articleTitle: Consolidation of a metro network into an access network based on long-reach DWDM-PON
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: We demonstrate bidirectional long-reach 35-channel DWDM-PON based on wavelength-locked Fabry-Perot laser diodes with 50 GHz channel spacing. The mode control of the Fabry-Perot laser diodes enhances output power and decreases the required injection power. We show packet-loss-free transmission of all 70 channels over 70 km single mode fiber without optical amplifier. The DWDM-PON can consolidate a metro network into an access network by bypassing the central office within the reach of the WDM-PON.

articleTitle: New details of spun fibers measured with an OFDR
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: OFDR signals from spun fibers contain frequency components related to a beating between effective beat length and spin period. Agreement between simulation and measured data allows correct extraction of spin period and effective beat length

articleTitle: Nonlinear optical fibers with increased SBS thresholds
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Novel profile designs are used to suppress stimulated Brillouin scattering in nonlinear fibers. The measured SBS thresholds of prototype fibers are 3 to 6 dB higher than those of conventional nonlinear fibers.

articleTitle: Demonstration of DPSK-OCDMA with balanced detection to improve MAI and beat noise tolerance in OCDMA system
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: For the first time, we demonstrate a coherent OCDMA experiment using differential phase-shift-keyed (DPSK) data format with balanced detection. More active users could be accommodated in DPSK-OCDMA due to its better tolerance to multiple access interference (MAI) and coherent beat noise.

articleTitle: SLiT: strongly connected light-trail for cost efficient and dynamic optical networking
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: In this paper we enhance the concept of a single unidirectional light-trail into a new concept called SLiT or strongly connected light-trails that improves utilization and lowers costs. We showcase architecture, performance and cost benefits.

articleTitle: A fully integrated block turbo code FEC for 10 Gb/s optical communication systems
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: A block turbo code FEC compatible with G.709 has been fully integrated on VLSI. Combining this with a 3-bit soft decision ASIC enabled a net coding gain of 10.1 dB at 12.4 Gb/s with 23.6% redundancy.

articleTitle: High-speed optical characterization of intensity and phase dynamics of a 1.55 /spl mu/m VCSEL for short-reach applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
abstract: Using sonograms and phase retrieval we experimentally investigate the pattern dependence of the amplitude and phase dynamics, the linewidth enhancement factor, and the chirp of a data-modulated 1.55 /spl mu/m vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL).

articleTitle: Optimizing system performance of free-space optical MIMO links with APD receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 Optical Fiber Communication Conference and the National Fiber Optic Engineers Conference
